## Amendment 399 (19 Sep 2026, 04:40) - THE MASS READING OF rho_0 IS DEAD, KILLED BY ITS OWN PRE-REGISTERED TEST;
## and the table it produced contains one number worth a second look, stated with its systematic.
(1) THE IDEA AND ITS TEST (q302). Writing the bulk law as rho^3 = B (d + d_0) with d_0 = rho_0^3 / B, the boundary
does exactly one thing to the bulk: it shifts the origin of the power law by d_0. If that shift is paid for by
the boundary layer's excess mass - the wall atom weighing more than a bulk cell, the first gaps being wider than
the bulk wants - then rho_0 follows from a mass balance and is derivable rather than fitted. Pre-registered: d_0
and L_mass = (excess mass)/(bulk mass density) must agree, channel by channel, with no free parameter.
(2) THEY DO NOT.
   Gaussian wall   d_0 = +1.1930   L_mass = 2.0156, 2.0132, 2.0132, 2.0141, 2.0155   ratio 1.688 - 1.690
   binomial wall   d_0 = +0.1925   L_mass = 2.0775, 2.0732, 2.0732, 2.0749, 2.0773   ratio 10.770 - 10.792
Not one, and not even the same ratio in the two channels. The mass reading is dead. The control behaved as a
control should: varying the layer depth over 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 atoms moves L_mass by 0.0024 (Gaussian) and
0.0043 (binomial), 0.2 %, so the layer is genuinely about four atoms deep and the disagreement is not a cut
artefact. This removes the most natural derivation route for rho_0, which is worth recording as such.
(3) L_mass IS STABLE BUT NOT YET AN INVARIANT. It sits at 2.014 (Gaussian) and 2.075 (binomial), each constant to
0.2 % across every certified state - n = 320 to 865, A = 21 to 46 - and the two differ by 3 %, which is fifteen
times that spread, so they are distinguishable. Both are near 2. I am NOT claiming that: L_mass depends on a
convention I chose, namely that the wall atom at d = 0 contributes its whole weight to an interval extending only
inward. Halving its share moves the Gaussian's value from 2.01 to about 0.49. Until the convention is fixed by
something other than my hand the number means nothing, and the "near 2" is not evidence.
(4) THE NUMBER WORTH A SECOND LOOK, with its systematic attached. d_0(Gaussian) - d_0(binomial) = 1.1930 - 0.1925
= 1.0005, and across all the certified states individually the difference runs 1.0015 to 1.0019. One Fisher unit.
But 393(3) measured the window systematic on rho_0^3 at 2 % (Gaussian) and 17 % (binomial), and d_0 inherits it,
so the honest statement is 1.002 +- 0.04. SUGGESTIVE, NOT ESTABLISHED - the systematic is twenty times the
apparent departure from one, and a difference of exactly one Fisher unit between two channels would need the
systematic beaten down by an order of magnitude before it could be claimed.
PRE-REGISTERED SHARPENING, cheap and already possible: the 17 % on the binomial comes from a short window on
short states. The n = 1112 run now going has 39 interior atoms against 33, which extends the usable window from
[8, 20] to about [8, 26] and should cut the systematic by roughly the square root of the atom count. If
d_0(G) - d_0(B) stays at 1.00 with a systematic of 0.01, it becomes a claim; if it moves, it was arithmetic.
Gates: no gate word used. (2) is a pre-registered kill. (3) refuses a number on the grounds that its convention is
mine. (4) states a coincidence, its size, and the measurement that would decide it.

## Amendment 401 (19 Sep 2026, 05:35) - THE FIRST POISSON RUN STALLED BECAUSE THE SOFT-MODE MACHINERY WAS NEVER
## SWITCHED ON: I passed the wrong environment variable. Diagnosed from the code, not from a theory.
(1) WHAT HAPPENED. The seed of 396(2) at A = 1139.935, K = 46 drove the residual from 1.381e-03 to 2.256e-07 in
fourteen Newton steps and then stopped. Its own history is the diagnosis:
   0.001381@1  1.174e-5@0.25  9.354e-6@0.5  7.278e-6@1  4.122e-7@0.1  3.845e-7@0.25 ...
   2.305e-7@0.01  2.285e-7@0.01  2.265e-7@0.01  2.256e-7@stuck
The number after the @ is the damping. It collapses to 0.01 and each step then gains about 1 % - which is what a
CORRECT descent direction gives at a 1 % step. So the direction is right and the line search refuses to take it
whole: the classic signature of a Newton step dominated by a near-null direction of an ill-conditioned Jacobian.
The seed is not at fault. It did its job - four orders of magnitude - and 396's construction stands.
(2) THE CAUSE, read from the source. support_mp3b and its copy support_mp4 take the SVD-capped step only when the
environment variable SVDCAP is set; SOLVER is what q206 (Gaussian) and q179 (binomial) read. I set SOLVER=svdls.
The module ignored it and used a plain lu_solve, so the machinery built precisely to handle the soft directions
was never engaged. Every Poisson run in this project's history used the same invocation, which is consistent
with the record that no Poisson state has ever been certified and that an earlier port "ran five hours without
finishing".
PROCESS RULE added: CHECK WHICH ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE THE MODULE ACTUALLY READS. Three different solvers in this
project take three different names for the same idea, and an unread variable fails silently - the run looks like
a solver ceiling.
(3) A SECOND READING OF THE SAME OUTPUT, and the same lesson as 398(4). The off-atom signal is +2.3209e-07 and
the residual is 2.256e-07. The signal is the size of the residual, so it says nothing about optimality and is not
evidence that the state is non-optimal. Minimum weight 0.01629 and the atoms ordered - both healthy.
(4) THE RESTART, with the cap chosen rather than copied. The solve vector concatenates weights (about 0.02) and
POSITIONS IN x (0 to 1140), so one cap governs two scales that differ by four orders of magnitude. q206's value
of 0.05 suits positions of order 50; at 1140 it is twenty times tighter in relative terms and would crawl. Set
SVDCAP=0.5, which lets an atom move 0.5 in x - at x = 1000 that is 0.016 in the Fisher coordinate, small but
useful - while still clipping the catastrophic component. Restarted from the saved 2.256e-07 state rather than
the seed, so the 1984 seconds already spent are kept.
(5) A TRAP NOTED IN PASSING. The results file stores x and w as forty-digit STRINGS, and support_mp4.solve reads
strings at full precision but floats at sixteen digits. The restart coerces to float for a diagnostic line, which
is harmless at 2e-07 and would silently throw away twenty-four digits if it were ever done to a converged state.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) and (2) follow the rule about reading a failed run's own lines and then its code;
(3) refuses to read a signal that is smaller than the residual it sits in.

## Amendment 402 (19 Sep 2026, 06:05) - PRE-REGISTRATION, written while only the first of four dark-current points
## exists, so the sharper prediction can still fail.
(1) THE FIRST POINT. q303 solves the dark-current Poisson as the plain Poisson on [lambda, A + lambda] with the
end atoms pinned (support_mp4's documented pin_ends), seeded from the archived K = 24 state shifted by lambda.
At lambda = 0.05, A_total = 385.680, residual 1.39e-07 after 30 steps:
   origin gaps  2.8254792  2.2092883  1.9569546  1.8048665
   wall gaps    2.7179421  2.1692853  1.9350138
Two things already check out. The origin gap lies strictly inside (2.7188433, 3.1256666) as 402's parent
prediction requires - it is 74 % of the way from the Poisson origin chain to the Gaussian one. And the FAR wall
gap is 2.7179421 against the lambda = 0 state's 2.7179421, identical to seven digits: adding a dark current at
one end leaves the other end untouched, which is 388's screening again and a control I did not arrange.
The residual is 1.39e-07, far above certification, so by 394(5) the chain is usable and nothing else is.
(2) THE SHARPER PREDICTION, pre-registered now. 394(3) measured the Poisson's own NOISY WALL approaching the
Gaussian chain from BELOW as 2.7188433 - 0.0177/sqrt(A). The dark-current ORIGIN approaches the same Gaussian
chain from ABOVE, because at large lambda the local channel is Poisson(lambda), Gaussian to relative order
1/sqrt(lambda). Both are the same expansion of the same channel about the same limit, differing only in which
side of the mean the boundary sits. So:
   PREDICTION A: gap_origin(lambda) - 2.7188433 = +c / sqrt(lambda) at large lambda, with c > 0;
   PREDICTION B (the sharp one): |c| equals the wall's 0.0177 to within the measurement, i.e. the two
   coefficients are equal and opposite.
B is the one worth having and the one that can fail. If |c| comes out at 0.018 the two boundaries of the Poisson
channel are the same expansion seen from two sides; if it comes out at 0.05 or 0.005 then B is dead while A may
survive, and the local-channel principle keeps only the weaker statement.
NOTE ON WHAT COUNTS AS LARGE: lambda = 0.05 is NOT in the asymptotic regime - 1/sqrt(lambda) = 4.47 there, and
naively extrapolating from that single point gives c = +0.0239, which is quoted here only to show that the point
is NOT being used for the test. The fit will use lambda = 2.0 and 8.0, with 0.5 as the consistency check.
(3) WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT THIRD CASE. 392 and 394 rested on two boundaries read off states that already existed.
The dark current is a CONTINUOUS family between them, run on purpose, with the interpolation, its endpoints and
now its approach rate all predicted in advance. A one-parameter family that lands on both endpoints and the
predicted rate is a different quality of evidence from two isolated agreements.
Gates: no gate word used. Nothing in (2) is claimed; it is written down so that the run can contradict it.

## Amendment 403 (19 Sep 2026, 06:55) - THREE ROUTES TO rho_0, ALL THREE DEAD. What survives is a second pair of
## boundary invariants and a sharper statement of why the constant is hard.
393(5) left "derive rho_0 for one channel" as the open problem and 399 killed the mass reading. Three more
candidates, each with its test run before it was written up:
(1) THE WALL ATOM'S WEIGHT. Its Voronoi cell is half the first gap, so the natural dimensionless quantity is
we / (pbar g_1 / 2), the wall atom's weight over what the bulk mass density would give that cell:
   Gaussian  2.5742, 2.5742, 2.5742, 2.5742, 2.5741, 2.5748   over K = 26 to 70
   binomial  2.5101, 2.5101, ... 2.5102                        over n = 320 to 865
Stable to five digits across every certified state - but the two channels differ by 2.5 % where rho_0^3 differs
by a FACTOR OF SIX (0.0233 against 0.0038). The wall atom's weight does not carry rho_0. DEAD as a route, and
recorded as a pair of invariants in its own right: unlike 399(3)'s L_mass, this one uses the atom's own cell
rather than a cut I chose, so the convention is not mine.
(2) THE ACCUMULATED GAP EXCESS over the pure power law. The asymptotics of a shifted power law say
sum(g_j - g_pure) -> -d_0, and at a cut of eight gaps the numbers looked close: -1.2718 against d_0 = +1.1912
(Gaussian), -0.1690 against +0.1893 (binomial), ratios 1.068 and 0.893. Varying the cut kills it:
   Gaussian  cut 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20  ->  -1.0586 -1.1839 -1.2718 -1.3389 -1.3928 -1.4374 -1.4753 -1.5363
   binomial                                   ->  -0.1421 -0.1595 -0.1690 -0.1738 -0.1753 -0.1743 -0.1713 -0.1609
The Gaussian's drifts monotonically through the target and keeps going (ratio 0.889 to 1.291); the binomial's
peaks at cut 12 and reverses. No convergence, so no quantity. The agreement at cut 8 was where I happened to cut.
The reason is in 385: the true bulk law DRIFTS (X = X_w + s d), so a comparison against a pure power law with one
fixed B accumulates the drift forever. Comparing against the drifting law instead would converge and would also
be circular, since that law already contains rho_0.
(3) THE CAPACITY. Only five of the certified states carry a C value and three of those are Gaussian at different
K, which is not enough to separate C's dependence on A from any dependence on rho_0. NOT TESTED, for lack of
data, rather than dead - recorded so it is not re-proposed as new.
(4) WHAT THIS NARROWS. rho_0 is not the wall atom's weight, not the boundary layer's excess mass (399), and not
the chain's accumulated displacement. Each of those is a LOCAL functional of the first few atoms, and each is
stable to four or five digits while failing to track rho_0 by factors of 2.5 to 6. That is itself informative:
the boundary constant is not a local functional of the boundary layer. It is the matching coefficient between a
semi-infinite boundary solution and a far field, which is what 393(5) said and what these three failures now
support rather than assume. The instrument that would settle it is the semi-infinite solve - one boundary, the
bulk law as the far field, rho_0 the eigenvalue - and that has not been built.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) and (2) are pre-registered tests that failed, with the numbers that killed them.
(3) says untested, not dead.

half-length is h = pi sqrt(n)/2:
   n = 865   h = 46.20   predicted sigma_min 2.1e-12
   n = 1112  h = 52.10   predicted sigma_min 1.5e-13
Fourteen times more ill-conditioned. Every binomial walk that converged with svdls sat at n <= 865. This is the

## Amendment 406 (19 Sep 2026, 08:55) - rho_0 MEASURED FROM THE EXACT ATOM POSITIONS INSTEAD OF FROM
## DIFFERENTIATED DENSITIES. The precision improves by an order of magnitude, the old values were BIASED by 3 %
## and 22 %, and 393's and 400's numbers are superseded.
(1) WHY THE OLD ESTIMATOR WAS COARSE. 393 fitted X = kappa_AM rho^4 rho'^2 in a window and integrated back to
d = 0. Both rho and rho' are FINITE DIFFERENCES of the gaps, so almost all of the forty digits the solver produces
are discarded before the fit begins, and the back-integration carries the model error across the whole window.
393(3) could only report 0.0233 +- 0.0005 (Gaussian) and 0.0038 +- 0.0006 (binomial) - two digits.
(2) THE NEW ESTIMATOR. The POSITIONS are exact. The same model
   rho^3(d) = rho_0^3 + (2/(s sqrt(kappa_AM)))[(X_w + s d)^(3/2) - X_w^(3/2)],  N(d) = int_0^d rho,
predicts every atom through N(d_j) = j - 1/2 + c, and (rho_0^3, X_w, s, c) are fitted to the positions by least
squares. The wall chain and the centre must be excluded, because 387(1) showed the bulk law describes neither -
fitting from atom 1 gives rms residuals of 3e-03 to 1.6e-02 atoms and rho_0^3 scattering from 0.010 to 0.036,
which is how that mistake announces itself. Fitting the BULK only, d in [8, 0.55 A]:

   binomial n = 658-679  0.0045817 to 0.0046028             n = 856-865  0.0046038 to 0.0046078
   rms residual 6e-07 to 6e-06 ATOMS - the model places every atom to within a millionth of a gap.
(3) THE CONTROL, which the old estimator never had. Building a comb whose positions come from the model exactly
and fitting it back:
   in  0.024020 / 1.73880 / -0.001582   out  0.024020 / 1.73880 / -0.001582   rms 6.2e-09, error -7.8e-08
   in  0.004650 / 1.72950 / -0.003528   out  0.004650 / 1.72950 / -0.003528   rms 6.3e-09, error +7.7e-09
   in  0.024000 / 1.74000 / -0.001000   out  0.024000 / 1.74000 / -0.001000   rms 6.8e-09, error +8.4e-08
Bias below 0.001 %, and unchanged when the positions are rounded to 1e-09. So the estimator is clean, and the
real states' rms of 6e-07 to 6e-06 is 100 to 1000 times the estimator's own floor - it is the MODEL's
inadequacy, not the fit's, which is a separate and useful fact about the drifting first integral.
(4) THE NUMBERS, superseding 393(2).
   rho_0^3 (Gaussian) = 0.02400 +- 0.00008   (the spread across states is 2e-05; the window systematic, from

The old values were 0.0233 and 0.0038 - low by 3 % and by 22 %. The binomial's was the worse because its window

(5) WHAT IT DOES TO 400. With d_0 = rho_0^3 / B and B = 3 sqrt(X_w/kappa_AM):
   d_0(Gaussian) = 1.22832 +- 0.00059 over K = 50, 60, 70

   difference at finite n = 860:  0.99177
400 reported 0.9966 at finite size and 1.0206 after extrapolating, and concluded the asymptotic difference sits

## Amendment 407 (19 Sep 2026, 09:25) - rho_0 IS NOT A WELL-DEFINED CONSTANT UNTIL THE EXACT BULK LAW IS KNOWN.
## 406(4)'s precision claim is corrected, and 393(5)'s open problem is restated in a form that is well posed.
(1) A READING OF MINE, KILLED BY ITS OWN TEST. The position-fit residuals oscillate - for the Gaussian K = 70,
-2.12 +2.11 +2.88 +0.71 -1.85 -3.10 -2.48 -0.37 +2.17 +3.65 +2.28 -3.88 in units of 1e-06 atoms - and the
binomial's have the same shape at 2.7 times the amplitude. They are identical from NG = 4000 to NG = 50000, so
they are in the data, not the quadrature. I read that as an oscillation of period about six atoms. It is not.
The sign-change count is FOUR in every state whether the window holds nine, ten or twelve atoms, which a fixed
period cannot do. Adding parameters settles it:
   parameters   4         5         6         7
   G K = 70     4 flips   5 flips   6 flips   7 flips     rms 2.5e-06, 6.7e-07, 2.0e-07, 4.1e-08
   B n = 865    4 flips   5 flips   6 flips   7 flips     rms 6.1e-06, 3.8e-07, 1.2e-07, 2.3e-08
The count tracks the parameter count exactly. That is the equioscillation of a least-squares misfit, not a
physical oscillation, and "period six atoms" is withdrawn before it was written anywhere but here.
(2) AND THE SAME TABLE CORRECTS 406(4). As the model gains parameters the fit improves by a factor of a HUNDRED
while rho_0^3 WANDERS:
   G K = 70   0.02401  0.02387  0.02405  0.02433     spread 1.9 %
   B n = 865  0.00460  0.00424  0.00435  0.00454     spread 8.5 %
406 quoted +- 0.00008 (0.3 %) from varying the window at FIXED model order. That understated the real
uncertainty, which is model order, not window. The honest values are
   rho_0^3 (Gaussian) = 0.0240 +- 0.0005   rho_0^3 (binomial) = 0.0046 +- 0.0004
So 406's gain is in the CENTRAL VALUE, not the precision: its estimator is verified unbiased on synthetic ground
truth to 0.001 % where 393's was biased low by 3 % and 22 %, but the number is still two digits.
(3) WHY, AND THIS IS THE POINT. rho_0 is the d -> 0 limit of the BULK law, and at d -> 0 the profile is not the
bulk law - it is the wall chain, which 387(1) showed departs from it by 33 %. So rho_0 is not a density anyone can
measure; it is a coefficient in a parametrisation, defined only as precisely as that parametrisation is correct.
Over a twelve-atom window several laws fit the exact positions to within a hundred-millionth of a gap and
extrapolate back to d = 0 two per cent apart. That is not a measurement problem and no estimator fixes it.
(4) THE OPEN PROBLEM, RESTATED. 393(5) said "derive rho_0 for one channel". That is ill posed, because rho_0
depends on the law it is a coefficient of. The well-posed version is: DERIVE THE EXACT BULK LAW - the function
X(d), of which 385's linear drift is the first two terms - and rho_0 follows from it as a by-product. The
evidence that this is the right statement is (2): every attempt to pin rho_0 without knowing the law moves it,
and 403 separately showed rho_0 is not a local functional of the boundary, so it cannot be got at from the wall
side either.
(5) WHAT WOULD MOVE IT. (a) A derivation of X(d) from the ripple functional, which is the only route that gives
the law rather than fitting it. (b) A semi-infinite solve in which rho_0 is an OUTPUT of the boundary problem
rather than an extrapolation of a fit - still worth building, but it inherits the same ambiguity unless its far
field is the exact law. (c) A very long profile: the degeneracy between rho_0 and the higher terms weakens as the
window's dynamic range in d grows, but K = 80 buys d_max = 28 against K = 70's 25, so this needs K of order 200,
not 100.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) kills a reading of mine with the test that distinguishes it; (2) corrects a
precision claim I made ninety minutes ago; (4) says an open problem I named was not well posed.

## determined to the fifth decimal where rho_0 is only two digits, and the universality statement moves from a

(1) THE OBJECT THAT IS WELL DETERMINED. 407 showed rho_0 wanders by 2 % as the model gains parameters while the

(2) THE TWO CHANNELS SHARE THE LAW. The binomial's X(d) rises with n at every d, and extrapolating in 1/n:
   d = 12   660: 1.67717   674: 1.67810   865: 1.68776   ->  1.72187   Gaussian 1.72001   difference +0.00186
   d = 14   ...                                          ->  1.71818   Gaussian 1.71662   difference +0.00156
   d = 16   ...                                          ->  1.71459   Gaussian 1.71329   difference +0.00131

At finite n the binomial sits about 2 % below the Gaussian; extrapolated, it lands within 0.01 % to 0.1 %. This
is the universality question asked of the whole bulk law instead of a single number, and the answer leans

(3) THE CAVEAT, which is the same one that has limited every binomial extrapolation today. The three sizes span

limit's own error is not quantified by three points, and the residual differences of 0.0001 to 0.0019 are between

(4) A STRUCTURE IN THE RESIDUAL DIFFERENCE, recorded without interpretation. The leftover difference falls

extrapolation error alone there is no reason for it to depend on d in an ordered way. MEASURE BEFORE NAMING A
MECHANISM applies: this is one state-triple and one fit, and nothing is claimed from it.
(5) WHAT THIS MAKES THE TARGET. 407(4) restated the open problem as "derive the exact bulk law X(d)". (1) now
supplies that law empirically, to the fifth decimal, for both channels, size-independent, in a form a derivation
can be checked against atom by atom - the same service the boundary chains performed for 392 and 394. The

## Amendment 415 (19 Sep 2026, 12:00) - A CORRECTION TO 414(5) AND THE FIX IT POINTED TO: the Poisson solver has
## NO soft-mode machinery at all, and its cap was being read in the wrong units.
(1) THE CORRECTION. 414(5) wrote that SVDCAP = 0.5 leaves "the soft-mode search mostly switched off", which
carries over 410(2)'s finding about q179. It does not apply: support_mp4 has NO soft-mode search to switch off.
Counting the machinery - soft_line_search, nested_cycle, nested_quadratic - q206 has seven occurrences, q179 has
seven, support_mp4 has ZERO. Its only tool is the bare SVD cap. That is the real reason every Poisson run in this
project's history has ended short, and it is a stronger statement than 401 made: 401 found the cap was never
switched on, and the truth is that even switched on it was the only thing there.
(2) THE SECOND DEFECT, which is the one worth fixing first. support_mp4 applies the cap to the RAW variables, and
the solve vector concatenates weights of order 0.02 with POSITIONS OF ORDER 1000. A single cap therefore cannot
mean the same thing for both: at SVDCAP = 0.05 it bites on every weight direction and no position direction, and
at 0.5 it bites on almost nothing (414's run). q179 solved this long ago by scaling the position columns before
the SVD - "one unit of the Fisher coordinate is sqrt(n)/2 counts", in its own words - so the cap is read in t
units. The Poisson's Fisher coordinate is t = 2 sqrt(x), so one Fisher unit at atom i is sqrt(x_i) in x.
(3) THE PORT (support_mp5). The position columns are scaled by sqrt(x_i) before the SVD and the step is unscaled
afterwards. With SVDCAP unset the code path is untouched, and the residual functions are unchanged - the archived
K = 24 state gives max|D_i - D_0| = 5.471910781074541802222177e-16 under both modules, identical to every printed
digit. Relaunched from the 4.814e-08 state with SVDCAP = 0.05, which in these units now means one twentieth of a
Fisher unit rather than one twentieth of an x-unit at x = 1000.
(4) WHAT THIS IS FOR. 414(2) returned UNDECIDED on the two-branch test because the bulk fit reached only 1.3e-03
atoms against the 1e-06 needed. That is a convergence problem, and (1) and (2) name why the convergence stopped.
If the state certifies, 409's question - is the bulk law a function of d or of rho - is answered with no
extrapolation at all, which is the only route to it that does not need a binomial at n far above 1112.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) corrects a sentence of mine from fifteen minutes ago by counting the code rather
than reasoning from a neighbouring solver.

## DENSITY MAXIMUM, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL. The two-branch verdict stays UNDECIDED, but 408's extrapolation is
## confirmed by direct measurement at two points.
(1) THE CAP WAS NOT THE ISSUE, as 415(4) pre-registered it might not be. With the Fisher-unit cap the trace reads
   it 1: 4.814e-8    it 2: 4.711e-8 [2 capped, lam 0.03]    it 3: 4.710e-8 [2 capped, lam 0.01]
   it 4: 4.708e-8 [2 capped, lam 0.01]

support_mp5 (415(1) established there was none) makes it fire - deltas 0.00193, 0.0017 - and recovers the descent
to about 1 % per step, but no more. The deltas are tiny against the 0.075 search range, so the soft direction is
not far off either. None of the three machinery fixes is the answer.
(2) WHERE THE RESIDUAL ACTUALLY LIVES. Decomposing the residual vector of the 4.814e-08 state: the eight largest
entries are ALL D-equality equations, at t = 37.03, 27.63, 38.22, 28.85, 26.39, 35.85, 25.12, 39.42, with the
density maximum at t = 32.97. Every one straddles the maximum; the two boundary regions are clean.
(3) AND THAT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A SEED DEFECT. At the density maximum rho' = 0, so X vanishes and the first
integral is degenerate: moving an atom there changes the neighbouring gaps symmetrically and D barely responds,
so those atoms are the weakest-determined in the state. The Gaussian and the binomial have no such region - their
profiles end at a REFLECTION POINT, where symmetry pins the centre exactly. The Poisson is the only channel with
an interior maximum, and that is why it is the only channel with no certified state. This is a statement about
the problem, not about the solver, and it is the first explanation the record has had for that gap.
(4) THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE TEST, and the measurement it rescues. If the floor is at the maximum, the branches'

(1) THE MEASUREMENT. Fitting N(d_j) = j - 1/2 + c with a smooth X(d) of npar parameters, on the bulk window:
   state      atoms   npar = 4   npar = 5   npar = 6   npar = 7

in ATOMS. The honest line is npar = 5 on K = 80: five parameters, fifteen atoms, ten degrees of freedom, residual

(2) WHY IT MATTERS. The record's standing account of the missing 40 % in the gradient coefficient (the passage

from the Poisson-summation form - the atoms are no longer at the integer crossings of a smooth cumulative

(4) THE POSITIVE CONTENT. If the comb is the integer-crossing set of a smooth density to 1e-06 of an atom, then
the Poisson-summation picture the ripple identity rests on is exact at the level anything else in this project is

## Amendment 424 (19 Sep 2026, 16:35) - 423's TENSION IS RESOLVED, THE EARLIER ACCOUNT STANDS, AND THE
## RECONCILIATION LICENCES A PURELY CONTINUUM DERIVATION. The scheduled read of 423(3), done.
(1) WHAT THE T-SERIES ACTUALLY IS. 423 flagged a tension with "the atoms are no longer at the integer crossings
of a smooth cumulative density: T5's ladder and the imposed-versus-relaxed gap (T4 vs T1) say this is where the
40 % lives", and scheduled a read before leaning on either. The T1-T6 in that sentence are NOT the count-law
series of Amendments 198-207; they are Amendment 349's list of targets a derivation must hit:
   (T1) the bulk profile obeys rho'' = b rho rho'^2 - 2 rho'^2/rho - b/(kappa_eff rho^3), kappa_eff/kappa_AM =
        0.648 - 0.047 g (Gaussian), 0.682 - 0.057 g (binomial), to 0.003
   (T3) along the profile kappa_AM rho^4 rho'^2 = 1.7-1.9 (Gaussian), 1.6-1.7 (binomial)
   (T4) an IMPOSED-position ramp at that amplitude costs 1.1 to 1.25 times the first-order gradient term
   (T5) the finite comb's central soft modes exceed the first-order functional's second variation by 1.60, 1.90,
        2.25, 2.58, 2.87, 3.14
   (T6) the weights are uniform density x cell to 3e-04
(2) SO THE CLAIM RESTS ON T4 AND T5, NOT ON A DISPLACEMENT. It compares an IMPOSED comb - positions taken from
one particular smooth density, the first-order one - with the RELAXED comb, and finds the relaxed one cheaper.
423 measured something different: whether the relaxed comb is the crossing set of ANY smooth density. Both can be
true, and 423(2) guessed exactly this. The resolution: relaxation does not take the comb off a smooth density, it
moves it from one smooth density to another. The earlier account stands; its wording invited the reading 423
gave it.
(3) AND THE RECONCILIATION IS WORTH MORE THAN THE TENSION WAS. If the relaxed comb is a smooth-density comb to
8.1e-07 of an atom (423(1)), then the entire 40 % lives in the CONTINUUM: it is the difference between two smooth
densities, not between a smooth density and a discrete correction to it. A derivation therefore needs no
discreteness term at all - it needs the right functional of a smooth density, whose minimiser is the measured
rho(d). That is a real narrowing of 422(4)'s "derive the form", and it is now supported rather than assumed.
(4) A CONSISTENCY CHECK BETWEEN THE OLD TARGETS AND THE NEW MEASUREMENTS. 349's (T3) recorded
kappa_AM rho^4 rho'^2 = 1.7-1.9 (Gaussian); 408 now measures that same quantity as X(d) = 1.70729 to 1.72001
over d = 12 to 20 - inside the old range and forty times tighter. And 349's (T1) coefficient makes
X(d) x kappa_eff/kappa_AM equal 0.98749 at d = 12 and 0.99855 at d = 20 - near one, as the Beltrami E = 0
condition would require, but drifting by 1.1 % across the window. That drift is 409's open question in another
guise, and the 0.648 - 0.047 g form was fitted to make the product one, so it cannot be used as evidence for it.
Gates: no gate word used. (2) withdraws 423's tension rather than the earlier account; (4) flags a circularity in
a fit I did not make and will not lean on.

## Amendment 425 (19 Sep 2026, 17:00) - THE EXACT RIPPLE, COMPUTED AT LAST, VINDICATES 364's FORMULA AND CORRECTS
## MY OWN 409. The gradient expansion is right; what was wrong is what I did with it.
(1) THE INSTRUMENT (q313). Everything in this project descends from the n = 1 ripple amplitude
a(y) = |int phi(s) exp(i theta(y+s)) ds| with theta = 2 pi N. 424(3) licensed a purely continuum treatment, and
406's fit gives N to 8.1e-07 of an atom, so a(y) can be computed EXACTLY by quadrature on the profile that
actually occurs, instead of expanded. CONTROL first: on uniform combs, where every gradient correction vanishes,
the exact a equals exp(-2 pi^2 rho^2) to 1.000000 at rho = 0.55, 0.64, 0.70, 0.75, with a spread over y of 1e-14.
(2) THE EXACT RIPPLE IS BARELY ENHANCED. On the certified K = 70 profile, exact a divided by its local value
exp(-2 pi^2 rho^2):
   d          10        12        14        16        18        20        22
   exact/lead 1.0399    1.0347    1.0307    1.0277    1.0253    1.0233    1.0217
Two to four per cent - eight per cent in the energy a^2 - where the Abbott-Machta gradient term at this profile's
X = 1.71 would make it sqrt(1 + X) = 1.65, a 65 % enhancement. The quadrature is not blind to gradients: forcing
a steeper ramp raises exact/lead to 1.155 at rho' = 0.02 and 6.46 at rho' = 0.08.
(3) AND 364's FORMULA IS RIGHT - VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED. Keeping its rho'' term explicitly,
|J|^2/lead^2 = 1 + ((b^2/3) rho^3 - b rho) rho'' + b(b rho^2 - 1/2) rho'^2:
   d              10        12        14        16        18        20        22
   exact/lead     1.039942  1.034661  1.030734  1.027699  1.025286  1.023331  1.021725
   364 with rho'' 1.038366  1.033478  1.029807  1.026949  1.024665  1.022805  1.021273
   ratio          1.00152   1.00114   1.00090   1.00073   1.00061   1.00051   1.00044
Agreement to between 0.04 % and 0.15 %, IMPROVING monotonically as the gradients fall - the signature of a
correct second-order expansion. 364 was never tested against the exact object until now.
(4) THE MECHANISM, and it is a cancellation. At the profile's own values the rho'^2 term alone gives
exact/lead = 1.066; adding the profile's own rho'' = -0.00035 pulls it to 1.040, and doubling rho'' pulls it to
1.014. So the curvature cancels most of the gradient enhancement. That is why the profile's ripple is nearly
local while its X = kappa_AM rho^4 rho'^2 is 1.71.
(5) THE CORRECTION TO 409, which is mine. 409 evaluated 364's BY-PARTS form - K_eff = kappa_AM rho^4 x bracket,
obtained by integrating the rho'' term against e^{-b rho^2} - as though it were a pointwise amplitude, and found
it eight times less flat than X. Column five above shows why: as a pointwise amplitude the by-parts form gives
1.539 to 1.577 against the exact 1.022 to 1.040, fifty per cent too large. By-parts is an identity for the
INTEGRAL, not for the integrand, so 409's test was mis-posed. 409's KILL OF THE BRACKET IS WITHDRAWN.
What 409 does still establish, read correctly, is the Beltrami statement: L_bp = P[1 + K_eff rho'^2] gives
P(K_eff rho'^2 - 1) = E, so K_eff rho'^2 = 1 + E/P; P = e^{-b rho^2} varies by 1e4 across the window while the
measured K_eff rho'^2 varies by 8 %, so E cannot be a constant. The profile is not an extremal of that
functional - which is 373's conclusion, reached independently and now on firmer ground.
(6) WHERE THIS LEAVES THE DERIVATION. The integrand is verified to 0.1 %; the profile is not its extremal. So the
missing piece is not the expansion but the VARIATIONAL PROBLEM - what is held fixed, and what the wall contributes
- which is exactly 373(5)'s open problem, now with a verified integrand to work with instead of a suspected one.
Gates: no gate word used. (3) is a verification of a formula that had never faced the exact object; (5) withdraws
a kill I made six hours ago, for a reason I can state exactly.

wrong profile's does not, at 2.3e-07 against F = 5.2e-02.
A BUG FOUND AND FIXED EN ROUTE, recorded because it inverted the answer: the first run evaluated a^2 only inside
the perturbed window and got derivatives LARGER on the certified profile than on the wrong one. The kernel reaches
+-9, so perturbing rho in [10, 24.1] changes a(y) well outside it; summing a^2 over [0.6, 33.6] is what the
constraint actually implies.
(2) WHAT IT WITHDRAWS. 373 concluded "the certified comb's bulk profile is not a stationary point of int |J|^2
under the count constraint", by two arguments: the Beltrami bracket of a TWO-TERM truncation does not vanish
along it, and no multiplier makes it consistent. 425(5) had already shown the by-parts form those arguments use
is not a valid pointwise object. (1) now tests the thing itself - the exact ripple energy, varied directly - and
it IS stationary. 373's conclusion is withdrawn. So is the open problem as 373(5) framed it: there is no missing
"wall contribution to the bulk equation" to find, because the bulk equation is satisfied.
(3) AND WHAT IT EXPLAINS. a(y) depends on N over a window of +-9 Fisher units, about nine atoms either side. The
functional is therefore NONLOCAL, and its Euler-Lagrange equation is an integro-differential equation, not an ODE
in rho and its derivatives. That is why:
   - no local first integral exists, so X = kappa_AM rho^4 rho'^2 DRIFTS (385) instead of being conserved;
   - every local expansion of the coefficient has failed at this amplitude (409, 425(5)) while the integrand
     itself is right to 0.1 % (425(3)) - localising a nonlocal functional is what breaks, not the expansion;
   - the "40 %" of 349's account is not a missing term but the difference between a nonlocal functional and its
     local truncation.
(4) WHAT IS NOW THE OPEN PROBLEM, restated for the third time today and much smaller than before. Not "derive
rho_0" (407 showed it ill posed), not "derive the wall's contribution" (2 removes it): SOLVE THE NONLOCAL
STATIONARITY CONDITION delta/delta rho int a^2 = mu for the profile shape, or show what its solution's X(d) is.
The functional is known exactly, the constraint is known, the solution is measured to five digits, and the test
above is the check any candidate must pass.
CAVEATS, stated plainly: m is held constant (uniform to 3e-04, so a correction of that order is unexamined);
three perturbation shapes, not a complete basis; the profile is the six-parameter fit of 406, which places every
atom to 2e-07; and the quadrature is float, with the eps-scaling rather than the absolute value carrying the
conclusion.
Gates: no gate word used. (2) withdraws a conclusion this project has carried since 17 September, on a direct
test of the object that conclusion was about.

## Amendment 428 (19 Sep 2026, 18:45) - THE POINTWISE FUNCTIONAL DERIVATIVE CANNOT BE MEASURED BY BUMPS ON THIS
## PROFILE. A negative with a clean reason, and 427 survives the challenge it raised.
(1) THE ATTEMPT (q315). 427's stationarity was established with three smooth perturbation shapes. The natural
strengthening is the pointwise condition delta F/delta rho (y) = mu, measured by perturbing rho with a narrow
bump at each y and dividing by the bump's integral. It gave a derivative that FALLS BY A FACTOR OF 200 from
y = 12 to y = 22, which would contradict 427 outright, since a varying derivative cannot integrate to zero
against every zero-integral perturbation.
(2) THE CONSISTENCY CHECK, which is what settled it. Taking 427's shape 1, whose count is preserved to 8.9e-16:
   directly measured dF/d(eps)             +1.7156e-09  (at eps = 5e-04, and falling as eps^2)
   predicted from the bump derivatives     +3.2774e-07
A factor of 190 apart, so one is wrong.
(3) IT IS THE BUMP. Its derivative does not converge as the bump narrows - at y = 12 it reads -1.115e-08,
-4.754e-08, -1.987e-07 for widths 1.5, 1.0, 0.7, growing roughly as the inverse fourth power of the width. A
valid functional derivative converges. The reason is 425(4): F depends strongly on rho'', and a Gaussian bump of
width w and height eps has rho'' = -eps/w^2 at its peak, so it is tiny in AMPLITUDE and huge in CURVATURE. At
y = 16, where the profile's own rho'' is -5.224e-04:
   width   induced rho''   ratio to the profile's   delta F/delta rho
   0.7     -2.041e-03      3.91                     -7.0924e-08
   1.0     -1.000e-03      1.91                     -1.0005e-08
   1.5     -4.444e-04      0.85                     -1.0308e-09
   2.5     -1.600e-04      0.31                     -7.3067e-10
   4.0     -6.250e-05      0.12                     -2.7565e-05   (edge effects: the bump leaves the window)
The derivative only settles once the bump is gentler in curvature than the profile itself - and by then the bump
is wide enough to stop being local, and soon after it runs into the window's edge. There is no width that is both
local and linear. THE MEASUREMENT IS ABANDONED, not the condition.
(4) SO 427 STANDS. Its perturbations span about fourteen units, so they induce rho'' of order eps (pi/L)^2 = 5e-05
against the profile's 5e-04 - a tenth, not four times - and its eps-scaling separates the linear term from the
rest explicitly, which is why its ratio of 4.00 is meaningful where a single bump's value is not.
(5) WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE DERIVATION. The Euler-Lagrange equation of the exact ripple energy must be obtained
ANALYTICALLY - by differentiating the ripple integral symbolically - not by numerical perturbation of this
profile. Numerical variation can only ever confirm a candidate (which q314 does, cheaply and decisively); it
cannot produce the equation. That is a genuine narrowing of how 427(4)'s open problem can be attacked.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) to (3) kill a measurement of mine within the hour of making it, by the consistency
check that (2) exists to provide.

## Amendment 429 (19 Sep 2026, 19:05) - THE BULK EQUATION, DERIVED IN CLOSED FORM AND CONFIRMED ON THE CERTIFIED
## PROFILE TO A RELATIVE ACCURACY OF 2e-05. This is the object the project has been looking for since 373(5).
(1) THE DERIVATION. With a(y)^2 = int int phi(s) phi(s') exp(2 pi i [N(y+s) - N(y+s')]) ds ds' and F = int a^2 dy,
vary N and shift y in each term so both delta N sit at the same point z. The double integral then depends only on
u = s - s' and collapses onto psi = phi (*) phi, the kernel's autocorrelation - for the unit Gaussian, a Gaussian
of variance 2 - and the two terms combine into a sine:
   delta F / delta N (z) = 4 pi int psi(u) sin(2 pi [N(z+u) - N(z)]) du.
Since N(z) = int_0^z rho, delta N(z)/delta rho(y) is a step, so delta F/delta rho (y) = int_y^inf delta F/delta N
dz; the count-constrained condition delta F/delta rho = mu therefore differentiates to
   E(z) := int psi(u) sin(2 pi [N(z+u) - N(z)]) du = 0.
A closed, nonlocal, integro-differential equation for the profile, with the channel entering only through psi.
(2) SANITY, before any state. A uniform comb has N(z+u) - N(z) = rho u, so the integrand is odd against an even
psi and E vanishes identically: computed, E = 0.0e+00, 1.4e-17, 1.4e-17, -2.8e-17 at rho = 0.55, 0.6364, 0.70,
0.7446, against a scale of 0.6366. So a uniform comb solves it exactly, as it must.
(3) THE TEST ON THE CERTIFIED PROFILE, against a deliberately wrong one (rho' scaled by 1.1):
   z          12           14           16           18           20
   certified  -4.98e-11    +4.67e-14    -6.83e-13    -1.73e-12    -1.75e-12
   wrong      +1.75e-08    +2.78e-09    +4.77e-10    +8.64e-11    +1.57e-11
(z = 10 and 12 sit within the kernel's reach of the fit window's edge and are not used.)
(4) HOW SMALL IS "ZERO" HERE - the sensitivity, which is what makes (3) a measurement. Scaling rho' by 1 + f:
   f          0.002        0.005        0.010        0.020        0.050
   E(16)      +8.49e-11    +2.00e-10    +3.61e-10    +5.84e-10    +7.59e-10
   E(16)/f    4.25e-08     4.01e-08     3.61e-08     2.92e-08     1.52e-08
Linear for f below about 1 %. The certified profile's E(16) = -6.8e-13 therefore corresponds to f = 1.6e-05: THE
PROFILE SATISFIES THE DERIVED EQUATION TO A RELATIVE ERROR OF TWO PARTS IN A HUNDRED THOUSAND IN ITS GRADIENT.
(5) THE FLOOR IS NOT THE PROFILE. Refitting with five, six and seven parameters moves the fit's own residual from
6.73e-07 to 1.98e-07 to 4.11e-08 atoms while E(16) stays at -1.57e-12, -6.81e-13, -1.69e-12. So the 1e-12 floor
is the quadrature and interpolation, not the state, and (4)'s 2e-05 is an upper bound on the profile's departure.
(6) WHAT IT CLOSES AND WHAT IT LEAVES. It closes 373(5), 407(4) and 427(4): the bulk equation is derived, in
closed form, with no free coefficient and no wall term - the channel enters only as psi. It does NOT yet give
X(d) in closed form; that requires solving E(z) = 0, which is the remaining work, and 408's five-digit X(d) is
the check. It also explains 422: no window could identify the form because the form is the solution of a nonlocal
equation, not a function from a short list.
CAVEATS, stated plainly. F = int a^2 keeps the deficit to second order in a; a is about 3e-04 here so the next
order is 1e-08 relative - negligible but not zero. The mass density m is held constant (349's T6: uniform to
3e-04). The profile is 406's fit, which places every atom to 4e-08. The test uses three interior z; the two
nearest the window edge are excluded and said so.
Gates: no gate word used. The derivation is elementary once the variation is taken at fixed z; what makes it a
result is (2), (4) and (5) - a sanity case that must vanish and does, a sensitivity that converts "small" into a
number, and a floor shown to belong to the instrument rather than the claim.

## Amendment 430 (19 Sep 2026, 19:25) - WHY EVERY LOCAL TREATMENT FAILED, NOW A NUMBER: the gradient expansion of
## the bulk equation is wrong by a factor of 2365 at second order, and still by 53 at fifth.
(1) THE MEASUREMENT. Truncating Delta(u) = N(z+u) - N(z) at successive orders in u inside
E(z) = int psi(u) sin(2 pi Delta(u)) du, on the certified profile at z = 16 (exact E = +4.011e-13):
   order 1  (rho u)            +1.39e-17    vanishes identically - odd integrand against an even kernel
   order 2  (+ rho' u^2/2)     -9.485e-10   2365 times the exact value
   order 3  (+ rho'' u^3/6)    +4.110e-10   1025 times
   order 4                     +6.417e-11    160 times
   order 5                     -2.141e-11     53 times
The same pattern at z = 14, 18 and 20. The signs alternate and the magnitude falls by only about three per order,
so ten or more orders would be needed to reach a factor of two.
(2) THE MECHANISM, and it is specific. E is the EVEN-in-u part of sin(2 pi Delta) integrated against psi; the
leading term is odd and cancels EXACTLY. So E is a small residual of large, nearly cancelling contributions, and
a relative error in the expansion is amplified by the ratio of the cancelling terms to what survives. The
AMPLITUDE has no such cancellation, which is why 425 found 364's second-order formula for a right to 0.04-0.15 %
while its second-order EL equation is out by three orders of magnitude. Those two facts are not in conflict: they
are the same expansion evaluated on quantities with and without a cancellation.
(3) WHAT IT EXPLAINS, quantitatively rather than by assertion. Abbott-Machta's functional, 364's kappa_eff, 349's
"missing 40 %", and every fitted effective coefficient in this project are second-order truncations of a
quantity whose second-order truncation is 2365 times too large. A 40 % discrepancy was never going to be
recovered by a better coefficient at that order - the order itself is the error. 427(3) said the failures were a
localisation error; (1) is the size of it.
(4) AND IT CONFIRMS 429 FROM A SECOND DIRECTION. The exact E on the certified profile is 4e-13, while every
truncation of it is between 2e-11 and 9e-10. If the exact E were merely small by accident, its truncations would
be small too. They are not: the profile satisfies the EXACT equation and no truncation of it, which is what a
genuine solution of a nonlocal equation looks like.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) is a measurement; (2) states a mechanism that (1) and 425 together force.

## Amendment 431 (19 Sep 2026, 19:35) - SOLVING E(z) = 0 IS NOT YET DONE, AND THE OBSTRUCTION IS THAT THE
## EQUATION ALONE DOES NOT DETERMINE THE PROFILE. Two attempts, both recorded.
(1) WHAT SELECTS THE SOLUTION IS NOT E = 0. A uniform comb satisfies E = 0 identically (429(2)), and in the bulk
the kernel never reaches the wall - psi(6) = 3.5e-05, psi(14) = 1.5e-21 - so E = 0 there cannot by itself pick the
ramp out of the family. The ramp must be selected by the TERMINATION (no atoms beyond the wall, so N is constant
for d < 0) together with the centre and the count. That is a two-point boundary value problem for a nonlocal
equation, which is a different and larger object than the equation itself.
(2) ATTEMPT ONE: the bulk form of 406 (five shape parameters), solving E = 0 at five z from 3 to 22 with
N(d < 0) = 0 and NOTHING else supplied. It converges - |E| from 2e-15 to 7e-11 - and lands in the right region:
   X(0) = 1.71082 against the measured X_w = 1.73595, 1.4 % low
   X(12) = 1.71354 against 1.72001, 0.38 % low
   gaps 3 to 6: 2.022, 1.847, 1.729, 1.641 against 1.935, 1.790, 1.687, 1.609 - within 3 to 4 %
but it FAILS on two things that matter: the slope comes out +0.0048 where the measurement is -0.0014, the wrong
SIGN, and the first gap is 1.442 against 2.71884. Both failures are where the bulk form is being asked to
represent the wall chain, which it cannot.
(3) ATTEMPT TWO: rho on fourteen free knots, E = 0 at fourteen z from 1 to 28. It does NOT converge - max |E| =
4.0e-04, median 7.3e-05, against 1e-11 in attempt one - and returns a profile with X(12) = 0.00014. Piecewise
linear knots give a rho with kinks, so rho' is discontinuous and E reads the kinks as structure; and with the
family of (1) the system is ill-conditioned.
(4) THE WALL ANATOMY. MATERIAL: E = 0 admits a family of solutions, so the solve is underdetermined without
boundary data, and E is sensitive to the smoothness of rho, so a knot representation injects false structure.
METHOD: least squares on E(z_i) = 0 with rho either in the five-parameter bulk form or on free knots. WHY HERE:
the bulk form cannot represent the wall chain and the free grid is not smooth enough. WHAT IS BEHIND IT: a C2
representation (a spline in rho^3) with enough freedom to carry both regions, the termination imposed exactly,
and the selector of (1) made explicit - most likely the count over [0, A] plus symmetry at the centre.
(5) WHAT STANDS REGARDLESS. 429's derivation and its confirmation to 2e-05 are untouched by this - they test
whether the MEASURED profile satisfies the equation, which it does. (2) is a weak, one-sided piece of evidence in
the same direction: an equation that knew nothing about the measurement produced X(0) within 1.4 % and four
chain gaps within 4 %, from the wall's termination alone. It is recorded as encouraging and NOT as a derivation
of X(d), because its slope has the wrong sign.
Gates: no gate word used. (3) reports a failed solve as a failure; (5) declines to read (2) as more than it is.

AMENDMENT 432 (q318_bulk_law_derived.py). THE BULK LAW DERIVED FROM THE EULER-LAGRANGE EQUATION ALONE, WITH NO
FITTED COEFFICIENT, AND CONFIRMED ON TWO CHANNELS TO 0.03-0.13 %.
(1) WHY 431 FAILED, AND IT WAS NOT THE REPRESENTATION. 431 blamed the parametrisation. That was wrong. The real
cause: E(z) = int psi(u) sin(2 pi [N(z+u) - N(z)]) du is EXPONENTIALLY SMALL FOR EVERY SMOOTH PROFILE. Measured
here directly - the wall taken from the certified state out to d = 10 and a CONSTANT X imposed beyond it, X swept
over a twentyfold range:
   X_bulk      0.5      1.0      1.5    1.72      2.0      3.0      5.0     10.0
   |E(18)|   3.0e-08  5.6e-09  6.2e-10 4.3e-11  4.0e-10  3.7e-10  3.3e-11  1.1e-11
against a scale int psi |sin| = 0.6366. Every one of them is "zero" at 1e-11. Least squares on |E| was therefore
not solving the equation; it was minimising exp(-4 pi^2 rho^2), which itself moves four orders across that sweep.
That is the whole of 431's failure, and no change of representation would have fixed it.
(2) THE CORRECTION. The ZERO of E is invariant under any positive normalisation, so ask where E CHANGES SIGN
rather than where it is small. Divided by its own scale the same sweep reads -1.06, -0.77, -0.56, +0.009, +0.33,
+1.11, ... - a single clean crossing.
(3) THE LAW. On the exact two-parameter family rho^3 = rho_c^3 + b u - constant X = kappa_AM (b/3)^2, NO wall and
NO termination anywhere - the phase is closed-form,
       N(z+u) - N(z) = (3/4b) [ (rho_c^3 + b u)^{4/3} - rho_c^4 ],
and at fixed rho_c the function E(X) crosses zero exactly once. That crossing X*(rho) IS the bulk law. Its only
inputs are kappa_AM = 128 pi^6/3 and psi = phi (*) phi (Gaussian of variance 2). Nothing measured enters.
   rho      0.61852  0.66689  0.69478  0.72058  0.74462  0.76719  0.78849  0.80869
   X*       1.724158 1.717984 1.714261 1.710866 1.707795 1.705022 1.702514 1.700232
(4) THE PRE-REGISTERED TEST, against 408's X(d), which played no part in any of the above. Gaussian K = 70:
    d       14        16        18        20        22        24        26
    X*    1.717984  1.714261  1.710866  1.707795  1.705022  1.702514  1.700232
    meas  1.716633  1.713296  1.710099  1.707147  1.704548  1.702408  1.700833
    diff  +0.079 %  +0.056 %  +0.045 %  +0.038 %  +0.028 %  +0.006 %  -0.035 %
  and the DRIFT, which 431's solve got with the wrong sign: derived -0.001479 per Fisher unit against a measured
  -0.001317 on the same window and 408's global fit of -0.00144.
(5) SELF-CONSISTENCY, since the family holds X constant over the kernel's reach while the true profile drifts.
Measured sensitivity at rho = 0.7446: dX*/d(slope in rho) = +0.0791, so the correction is real and the level and
the drift must be solved TOGETHER. Doing that - E = 0 at two densities at once, solving for (X0, dX/drho), still

    anchors rho = 0.6949, 0.7672 -> X(0.7310) = 1.710151, dX/dd = -0.001502
    anchors rho = 0.6669, 0.7885 -> X(0.7277) = 1.709781, dX/dd = -0.001523
    anchors rho = 0.7206, 0.7885 -> X(0.7546) = 1.707013, dX/dd = -0.001416
  against a measured 1.708819, 1.709225, 1.705922 at those rho and -0.00144: +0.078 %, +0.033 %, +0.064 %.
(6) THE CROSS-CHANNEL TEST, which the derivation predicts must pass because the channel enters ONLY through psi,
and psi is the same unit-Gaussian autocorrelation in Fisher coordinates for all three channels. Seventeen
certified OPTIMAL binomial states (residual < 1e-20, n = 658 to 865), Fisher coordinate d = pi sqrt(n) - 2 sqrt(n)
asin(sqrt(x/n)), window [8, 0.55 h] with h = pi sqrt(n)/2 so it stops short of the centre. Their rho(12) is
identical to 1.2e-04 across all seventeen, and X(12) is strictly linear in 1/n:
       X(12) = 1.721945 - 29.573/n,  residuals 3e-06 over the whole set.
  Extrapolated to n -> infinity: 1.721945 at rho = 0.61852. DERIVED: 1.724158. Difference +0.128 %.
  Gaussian at the same d: X(12) is size-INDEPENDENT at 1.719950 +- 2e-05 over six certified states
  (A = 35.55 to 46.38); derived 1.721966 at its own rho = 0.63641, difference +0.117 %.
  Two different channels, the same law, the same offset.
(7) CONTROLS, each able to fail and none of which did. (a) A uniform comb returns E = 1.4e-17, machine zero, as
the odd-integrand argument requires. (b) The crossing X* = 1.708592 is stable to six decimals across UMAX 12 to
14 and NU 8001 to 64001 - the 11-digit cancellation is being computed reliably, as a trapezoid on a
Gaussian-damped oscillation should. (c) The closed-form phase agrees with direct numerical integration of rho to
1.7e-09. (d) The crossing is unique: E/scale runs monotonically -0.91 at X = 0.8 to +0.80 at X = 2.5. (e) The
Euler march used for (5) reproduces the closed-form crossing to 0.001 % at zero slope. (f) A deliberately wrong
profile (rho' scaled by 1.1, so X scaled by 1.21) is rejected at -17.3 % where the true one is accepted at
+0.045 %.
(8) VALIDITY, stated as a condition and not as a caveat. The trial family's own density reaches zero at
u = -rho^3/b, so X*(rho) is defined only where that lies outside the kernel's reach - which is exactly the
statement that the kernel does not touch the wall. For the Gaussian K = 70 state that is d >~ 13; at d = 12 the
family is marginal (rho^3/b = 12.28 against a reach of 12), which is why (6)'s Gaussian entry is quoted with its
binomial counterpart rather than alone.
(9) WHY EVERY LOCAL TREATMENT IN THIS PROJECT FAILED, now with a reason rather than a symptom. The ripple
amplitude is a ~ exp(-2 pi^2 rho^2); E's natural size is exp(-4 pi^2 rho^2) = a^2. The stationarity condition
therefore lives at SECOND order in the ripple amplitude, so an order-2 truncation of |J|^2 (373) cannot see it at
all - which is what 431 measured as "the truncation is 2365 times the exact E" without knowing why.
(10) WHAT IS NOT EXPLAINED. Both channels sit +0.12 % BELOW the derived law at d = 12, and the Gaussian residual
falls monotonically from +0.079 % at d = 14 to -0.035 % at d = 26. That trend is not yet attributed. The
candidates, in order of my estimate: the constant-X family's window error (partly removed in (5), which moved
+0.045 % to +0.033 % at one anchor and to +0.078 % at another - i.e. it does not settle it); the assumption that
the mass density m(y) is uniform, which 349's T6 measured only to 3e-04, the same order as the discrepancy; and
the finite size of the states at d >~ 0.5 A. Until one of those is measured the law stands at the 0.1 % level and
NOT better, and that is how it is quoted.
Gates: no gate word used. The result is stated as a derivation agreeing with measurement to 0.03-0.13 %, with the
unexplained residual named in (10) rather than absorbed.

   wrong    -1.065   -0.606  +0.421  +0.817  +0.111  -0.580  -0.174  +0.286  +0.223  +2.8e-1 +2.0e-1 +1.2e-1
  In the bulk the equation VANISHES on the true profile (1e-04) and does not on the wrong one (0.1 to 0.3) - 429
  reconfirmed, and it discriminates by three orders. Near the wall it does neither: E is O(0.1 to 1) on the true
  profile and INDISTINGUISHABLE from the wrong one. E = 0 is therefore a BULK equation, and within the kernel's
  reach of the termination it is missing a term. The crossover is exactly where the wall term overtakes the bulk
  term: at z = 6 the kernel mass on d < 0 is 1.1e-05 against a bulk scale of 2.2e-05; at z = 8 it is 7.7e-09
  against 3.4e-06.
(5) THIS ALSO EXPLAINS 431 ATTEMPT ONE. It imposed E = 0 at z = 3 and 7.75, inside the region where (4) now shows
the equation is false, and let those corrupt the bulk parameters. Its wrong-sign slope was not a representation
failure; it was a false equation imposed in the wrong place.
(6) WALL ANATOMY. MATERIAL: the stationarity condition was derived by free variation of N with a constant count
multiplier; at the support's edge the variation is one-sided, so the condition becomes a KKT inequality with
complementary slackness rather than an equality, and the mass density m(y) - taken constant on 349's T6, which
measured uniformity in the BULK - has no such warrant near the wall. METHOD: evaluate E on a profile certified to
6.7e-07 of an atom, normalised by the local scale, against a wrong-profile control. WHY HERE: within the kernel's
reach of d = 0 the wall term is the LARGEST term in E and nothing in the derivation cancels it. WHAT IS BEHIND
IT: the boundary term. Three candidates, in the order I will test them - (a) the one-sided variation, i.e. redo
the derivation with the support constraint active and see whether the extra term is the observed residual;
(b) m(y) near the wall, measurable directly on the certified states the way T6 measured it in the bulk;
(c) the identification of the entropy deficit with int m a^2, which may itself carry a boundary term.
(7) WHAT 432 KEEPS. Nothing here touches it. 432's law was derived on a family with NO wall anywhere, and tested
at rho where the kernel does not reach the termination; (4) confirms the equation is exact precisely in that
region. The near-wall failure is a different region, now located to within one atom.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) is stated as a measurement of an extrapolation, (3) as a failure, (4) as the reason
for it, and (6) names what is behind the wall instead of stopping at it.

AMENDMENT 434 (q320_mass_weighted_el.py and the count probe). THE MASS DENSITY IS NOT THE BOUNDARY TERM; AND THE
DERIVED LAW INTEGRATES CORRECTLY OVER THE WHOLE RANGE, SO THE SUPPORT SIZE NEEDS ONLY A THRESHOLD.
(1) THE BOUNDARY TERM, DERIVED RATHER THAN GUESSED. 429 took the mass density m(y) constant. Redoing the
variation without that: with F = int m(y) a(y)^2 dy, substituting y = z-s, u = s'-s in one term and y = z-s',
u = s-s' in the other, both inner integrals collapse onto the SAME object and
      delta F / delta N (z) = 4 pi int Psi(z,u) sin(2 pi [N(z+u) - N(z)]) du,
      Psi(z,u) = int m(z-s) phi(s) phi(s+u) ds.
For constant m this is m psi(u), even in u, recovering 429. For varying m it is NOT EVEN IN u, and that odd part
is a term nothing cancels - which is the right shape for a boundary term, since m must fall off at the wall.
(2) IT IS NOT THE ANSWER. m is read off the state as m = w rho and fitted smoothly (rms 3.1e-03 relative over 34
atoms; a piecewise-linear interpolation through the atoms will NOT do - its kinks destroyed the bulk cancellation
entirely, giving E/scale = -0.33 at z = 8 where the truth is -1.6e-04, and that was a numerical artefact of mine,
not a result). CONTROL, which must pass first: in the bulk, where m is uniform, the weighted kernel reproduces
429's - ratio 0.9905 at z = 14 and 1.0005 at z = 18. It does. Then:
      z          1.5      2.0      2.5      3.0      3.5      4.0      5.0      6.0      8.0
   429       -0.644   +0.339   +0.789   +0.182   -0.563   -0.336   +0.298   -0.105  -1.6e-04
   weighted  -0.578   +0.165   +0.704   +0.206   -0.542   -0.338   +0.298   -0.106  -1.5e-04
  The mass weighting changes nothing near the wall. Reason, measured: the smooth m is uniform to 0.3 % down to
  d = 1 - it simply does not vary enough. 433(6) candidate (b) is KILLED, and (c) is killed in the form "m carries
  the boundary term". What remains of 433(6) is (a), the one-sided variation at the support's edge, and the
  identification of the entropy deficit with int m a^2 near the edge of the distribution, where the output density
  is a decaying tail rather than an envelope times (1 + ripple).
(3) THE SUPPORT-SIZE ROUTE, which needs no near-wall theory. If 432's law gives rho(d) and rho_0^3 is one
constant, then N(A) = int_0^A rho counts the atoms. Test against every certified Gaussian state, rho_0^3 = 0.02387
FIXED, the counts playing no part:
      A         21.2821  29.8500  35.5500  35.6000  35.6500  40.9500  41.0800  46.3837
   N(A) derived 12.5740  19.4631  24.4219  24.4666  24.5113  29.3616  29.4833  34.5484

(4) WHAT IS MISSING IS A THRESHOLD, NOT A LAW. N(A) - n_half is NOT constant: it runs 0.341 to 0.526 over these

That is now the cheapest remaining step to the support-size function, and it is a solver run, not an idea.
(5) rho_0^3 TIGHTENED. Fitted independently on eight certified states: 0.02382, spread 0.00030 (407 had

Gates: no gate word used. (2) kills my own candidate and labels my own numerical artefact as such; (4) states

AMENDMENT 437. THE EXACT STATIONARITY CONDITION, VALID AT THE WALL - AND THE BOUNDARY TERM IDENTIFIED AS THE
EDGE ATOM'S ANOMALOUS MASS.
(1) THE EXACT CONDITION, WITH NO EXPANSION ANYWHERE. The capacity KKT equality is i(x;Y) = C at every support
point, i(x;Y) = int phi(y-x) log(phi(y-x)/p(y)) dy with p = sum_j w_j phi(. - x_j). Differentiating in x, the
phi log phi part is constant, so
        d/dx (phi (*) log p)(x) = 0  at every INTERIOR atom.
No ripple, no smooth density, no truncation - it holds at the wall exactly as in the bulk, which is precisely
what E(z) = 0 does not (433(4)).
(2) VERIFIED ON THE CERTIFIED K = 70 STATE, grid-converged (stable from NY = 8e05 to 1.6e06):
     d from wall   2.71884    4.88844    6.82360    8.61375    deep bulk
     L'(x_j)      -7.49e-08  -8.96e-09  -2.79e-09  -7.91e-10   5e-10 and below
  against a scale of 2.221e-03, the mean |L'| at the midpoints BETWEEN atoms - so 3.4e-05 relative at the first
  interior atom falling to 2e-07 in the bulk. CONTROL: the same quantity at non-atoms does not vanish - ratio 33
  at d = 1.36 and 0.71 at d = 3.80 - so the test discriminates by two to four orders at every atom.
(3) A CORRECTION TO MY OWN HANDLING. These state files store the boundary atoms at +-A separately, as "we", NOT
in the "u" list. My first run of (2) omitted them, and with them missing the two atoms nearest the wall showed
violations of 3.3 and 188 times the scale - which I was one step from reading as a failure of the condition. It
was my own data handling. Every analysis in this record that used "u" alone for the ATOM POSITIONS is unaffected
(the interior chain is what it fits), but any statement about the mass near the wall that ignored "we" is not.
(4) THE EDGE ATOM'S CONDITION IS ONE-SIDED, AND IS NOT ZERO: L'(A) = -0.286. That is correct and required - the
edge atom sits at the boundary of the permitted interval, so its KKT condition is an inequality, not an equality.
(5) THE BOUNDARY TERM, IDENTIFIED. The edge atom's weight against a bulk atom's:
     Gaussian K = 70   we/w_bulk = 2.898       Gaussian K = 60   2.772       binomial n = 860   3.182
  Three states, two channels: the boundary carries about three times a bulk atom's mass in a single atom. A
  smooth density with m = w rho cannot represent that, which is why (i) E(z) = 0 fails inside the kernel's reach
  of the wall and (ii) 434(2)'s mass weighting did not repair it - the missing mass is a DELTA, not a profile.
  433(6)'s candidate (a) is thereby superseded: the boundary term is not a subtlety of the variation, it is an
  object the smooth description does not contain.
(6) WHAT THIS OPENS. rho_0^3 is the last underived constant (435(4)). The exact condition of (1) is valid at the
wall, so it can be attacked directly - the first few atoms plus the edge atom explicit, the bulk supplied by
432/435's derived law - instead of through the smooth-density equation that breaks there. That is the next
computation, and it is now a well-posed one.
Gates: no gate word used. (3) records my own error as mine; (5) states an identification supported by three
states and does not yet claim the derivation it enables.

AMENDMENT 439. THE EXACT KKT SYSTEM VERIFIED IN FULL; AND THE BARRIER AGAINST A NEW ATOM OBEYS THE SCREENING LAW
OVER SEVENTEEN ORDERS.
(1) THE SYSTEM, in one object. With L(x) := (phi (*) log p)(x) and p = sum_j w_j phi(. - x_j), the information
density is i(x;Y) = -h(phi) - L(x), so the whole KKT system reads:
     L(x_j) = L_0 at every support point   (the WEIGHT half)
     L'(x_j) = 0 at every INTERIOR atom, one-sided at the edge   (the POSITION half)
     L(x) > L_0 off the support             (the support points are MINIMA of L)
  Verified on the certified K = 70 state by direct quadrature (converged over SMAX 10 to 16, NS 2e04 to 1.6e05):
  L = -4.572120078080 at ALL thirty-five support points INCLUDING THE EDGE ATOM, agreeing to 1e-15; L' = 0 at the
  interior atoms to 7.5e-08 absolute against a between-atom scale of 2.2e-03; and L - L_0 > 0 at every midpoint.
(2) TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN WORK IN THE LAST HOUR, both caught by controls rather than by reasoning.
  (a) Computing L with np.convolve(..., mode="same") zero-pads near the domain edge, which put the EDGE atom
      2.57e-05 off the interior constant. I was one step from recording that as a real one-sided violation.
      Direct quadrature shows it is exact to 1e-15. Any L computed by grid convolution near a boundary is wrong.
  (b) I wrote the off-support control as "must be <= 0". The sign is the other way: i = -h(phi) - L, so KKT's
      i <= C off the support means L >= L_0 there. The support points are minima, not maxima, of L, and the
      +4.897e-02 I had flagged as a violation was the condition being SATISFIED.
(3) THE BARRIER, AND WHY THE NEW ATOM APPEARS AT THE CENTRE. The barrier against inserting an atom is
L(midpoint) - L_0, and it collapses monotonically from the wall to the centre:
     d        3.80      9.46     14.20     18.49     22.50     26.28     29.90     33.39     36.76
   barrier  1.52e-03  5.02e-06  1.01e-07  4.22e-09  2.73e-10  2.36e-11  2.53e-12  3.22e-13  4.62e-14
  Seventeen orders from d = 1.36 (4.90e-02) to the centre (1.78e-15). THAT is the mechanism of 438(3): the centre
  is simply where the barrier is weakest, so that is where an atom nucleates as A grows. The nucleation site was
  an observation; it is now a consequence of a measured profile.
(4) AND IT IS THE SCREENING LAW. Fitting -ln(barrier) against d^alpha over d = 3.8 to 36.8:
     alpha = 2/3  rms 0.0061      alpha = 1/2  rms 0.3538      alpha = 1  rms 0.6388
  The 2/3 form wins by a factor of sixty, and it is exactly the screening form: exp(-k int dd/rho) with
  rho^3 = B d gives exp(-(3/2)(k/B^(1/3)) d^(2/3)). Measured coefficient 2.8103 +- (rms 0.0061), against 2.5281
  predicted from the soft-mode rate k = 0.4525 +- 0.0070 - a ratio of 1.1117. Inverted, the barrier's own rate is
  k_barrier = 0.5034, against the soft mode's 0.4525. SAME EXPONENT AND SAME MECHANISM, RATES 11 % APART. Whether
  they are the same constant is NOT settled here: my fit used rho^3 = B d with B from X at d = 20 and dropped
  rho_0^3, whose inclusion shifts the fit, and k_barrier = 0.5034 sits 0.7 % from 1/2, which is a candidate
  closed form and nothing more until the fit is redone with rho^3 = rho_0^3 + B d and a drifting B.
Gates: no gate word used. (2) records two of my own errors; (4) names a candidate closed form and refuses it.

AMENDMENT 440. 439(4)'s PRE-REGISTERED REFINEMENT, RUN: THE CANDIDATE CLOSED FORM IS NOT SUPPORTED.
439(4) registered the test - redo the barrier fit against the EXACT screening integral int_0^d dd/rho, built from
the state's own fitted profile (so rho_0^3 and the drift of X are both carried), instead of the rho^3 = B d
approximation that produced d^(2/3). Run:
     -ln(barrier) = k int dd/rho + const:   k_barrier = 0.51611,  rms residual 0.05353
     -ln(barrier) = c d^(2/3) + const:      c = 2.8103 (k = 0.5034),  rms residual 0.00610
TWO THINGS FAIL AT ONCE, and both are recorded as failures.
(1) k_barrier = 0.51611 sits 3.2 % from 1/2, against 0.7 % for the cruder fit. Refining the instrument moved the
number AWAY from the candidate closed form, so 1/2 is NOT supported and 439(4)'s candidate is withdrawn.
(2) The EXACT integral fits WORSE than the approximation it was meant to improve - rms 0.0535 against 0.0061, a
factor of nine - and its residuals bow systematically: -0.19, +0.04, +0.06, +0.04, +0.01, -0.02, -0.05 across
d = 3.8 to 36.8. A form that fits worse when made exact is not the right form. So barrier = const x
exp(-k int dd/rho) is wrong as it stands; something multiplies it. A prefactor rho^a would add a ln rho drift,
and over this range ln rho moves by 0.69 while the bow is about 0.25, so a ~ -0.36 - which is not a recognisable
number and is offered only as the scale of what is missing.
(3) WHAT SURVIVES. The barrier decays exponentially over seventeen orders with an exponent that is d^(2/3) to
0.006 in -ln over a range of 25 - that stands, and so does 439(3)'s mechanism for the nucleation site. What does
NOT stand is the identification of the barrier's rate with the soft-mode screening rate: 0.516 against 0.4525 is
a ratio of 1.14, and the two are different constants unless the missing prefactor of (2) accounts for it.
Gates: no gate word used. The amendment withdraws my own candidate and records a fit that got worse.

(2) WHAT THIS SAYS, AND IT IS NOT WHAT I EXPECTED. The CHAIN improves by a factor of two to three (best -0.076
to -0.120 %, degree 3) while rho_0^3 gets WORSE, moving from -0.20 % to +1.15 to +2.90 %. They anticorrelate
because rho_0^3 and the quantisation offset c0 both shift N uniformly near the wall and the two atoms used cannot
separate them. So 438(2)'s rho_0^3 = 0.023823 was NOT a 0.20 % determination - it was one draw from a family
spanning 0.0238 to 0.0246. Against the measurement 0.02382 +- 0.00030 (+-1.3 %) the derived value is CONSISTENT
and no sharper. 438(2)'s headline figure is corrected accordingly: this route determines the CHAIN, not rho_0^3.

worse than 2.0e-03 (0.84, degree 3) - so the fit's DEGREE, i.e. how well it carries the curvature of X*(rho),
matters more than its residual, and neither explains a one-signed offset.
(4) THE LIKELIEST CAUSE IS ONE THIS RECORD ALREADY NAMED. 432(8) stated the validity condition of X*(rho)
explicitly: it is defined only where the trial family's own density stays positive across the kernel's reach,
which is exactly where the kernel does NOT touch the wall - d >~ 13 for this state. Building the chain requires
X all the way to d = 0, so every variant above EXTRAPOLATES the derived law into precisely the region 433(4)
showed the smooth-density equation fails. The -0.1 % is therefore the expected size of that extrapolation error,
and it is the same wall as 433(4) and 437(5), not a new one. It will not be removed by better fitting.
(5) PRE-REGISTERED CONSEQUENCE. If (4) is right, the chain error must SHRINK when the wall region is given its
own treatment - the weight half of the system solved rather than supplied - and must NOT shrink under any further
refinement of the bulk fit. The second half of that is already evidence: three refinements moved the error by a
factor of two and never changed its sign.

to a wall this record had already located rather than to a new effect.

  PARAMETER-FREE, which 448(1)'s version was not.
(3) THE HONEST LIMIT, which is now the instrument and not the theory. The iteration does not settle to machine
precision: max |dc| wanders between 2.3e-07 and 1.3e-06, and X*(20) moves over 1.706828 to 1.706908 across the
last iterations, a spread of 8e-05 - 0.005 %. That is the same 5e-05-in-X precision of 432(7) showing through. So
the agreement in (2), rms 0.0059 %, IS AT THE LEVEL OF THE METHOD'S OWN JITTER. The correct statement is that the
derived law and the measurement agree to within the precision at which either can currently be computed, and no
residual is resolved. Going further needs extended-precision arithmetic in the E quadrature, not a better fixed
point.
(4) WHAT THE NUMBER IS, FINALLY. The bulk law derived from the exact ripple energy, with kappa_AM and psi as its
only inputs and every coefficient self-consistent, reproduces the measured X(d) on the Gaussian to an rms of
0.006 % over d = 14 to 24. 447(4)'s 0.03 % residual, which two channels agreed on, is accounted for: it was the
trial family truncated at one coefficient. This supersedes 435(2), 436(1), 447(3) and 448(5) as the statement of
accuracy.
(5) STILL TO DO ON THIS THREAD. The binomial has not been redone at two coefficients - 447(3)'s -0.027 % is a
one-coefficient number and should move the same way. That is the cheapest remaining check of the whole
derivation, and it is a cross-channel one.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) records a divergence and its measured cause; (3) declines to claim a residual that
the method cannot resolve.

AMENDMENT 450. 449(5)'s CROSS-CHANNEL CHECK IS INCONCLUSIVE, AND THE REASON IS A SCISSORS BETWEEN TWO VALIDITY
CONDITIONS RATHER THAN A DISAGREEMENT.
(1) THE RUN. The fixed point of 449 re-parametrised in rho (c and e are universal functions of rho, since the
d-map cancels: drho/dd = sqrt(X/kappa_AM)/rho^2), converged over rho in [0.6205, 0.800] to max |dc| = 2.0e-08,
giving c = -5.393e-06 and e = +1.810e-08 at the binomial's rho(12) = 0.61988. Then:
     X* one coefficient  = 1.722268        X* two coefficients = 1.722340
     vs quadratic 1/n over n >= 658 (1.722701):   -0.0251 % -> -0.0210 %
     vs quadratic 1/n over all 18    (1.722721):  -0.0263 % -> -0.0221 %
  The second coefficient moves the binomial by only 0.004 %, where on the Gaussian it moved things from 0.021 %
  to 0.006 %. The binomial residual does NOT close.
(2) WHY, AND IT IS A SCISSORS. The binomial comparison can only be made at d = 12, because that is the only depth
where the n = 320 state's window reaches and therefore the only place the 1/n lever is long enough to determine
the extrapolation (447(2)). But d = 12 is exactly where the trial family is MARGINAL for the binomial:
rho(12) = 0.61988 gives rho^3/b = 12.3 against a kernel reach of 12, so the family's own density very nearly
terminates inside the kernel - the condition 432(8) states. At d >= 16, where the family is safe, only the short
lever exists (n = 658 to 865) and linear versus quadratic extrapolation differ by 0.044 %, eight times the effect
being tested. The two validity conditions - long 1/n lever, and family safely inside its reach - have no overlap
in the certified binomial set.
(3) SO THE CROSS-CHANNEL CHECK AT 0.006 % IS NOT AVAILABLE FROM EXISTING DATA, and 449(4)'s number stands on the
Gaussian alone. What 447(4) established - that both channels see the SAME 0.02-0.03 % one-coefficient residual -
is unaffected and remains the cross-channel evidence.
(4) WALL ANATOMY. MATERIAL: no binomial depth simultaneously satisfies both validity conditions. METHOD: the two-
coefficient fixed point in rho, evaluated at the extrapolated rho. WHY HERE: the certified binomial family spans
n = 320 then jumps to 658-865, so the lever is long only at small d, while the family needs large d. WHAT IS
BEHIND IT: a certified binomial state at an intermediate n - roughly 430 to 520 - whose window would reach
d ~ 18 while keeping the 1/n lever long. That is a solver run at an atom count between K = 17 and K = 27, which
is well inside the range the solver already handles, and it is the cheapest thing that would settle this.
Gates: no gate word used. (3) declines to claim a cross-channel figure the data cannot support.

AMENDMENT 451. THE FIVE-GATES LITERATURE CHECK I OWED, RUN: ABBOTT-MACHTA DO WRITE AN EULER-LAGRANGE EQUATION,
AND IT GIVES X = 1 EXACTLY WHERE THE CERTIFIED STATES GIVE 1.707.
(1) WHY THIS WAS OVERDUE. 432-449 derived a bulk law and I had not once compared it against the EL equation in
the source paper, because I had been carrying the belief - from 356 and 409 - that the two-term Abbott-Machta
functional "cannot predict a shape". That belief was about FITTING kappa_eff. It is not the same statement as
"their paper contains no density equation", and the second is false.
(2) WHAT THE PAPER CONTAINS. Abbott and Machta, J. Stat. Phys. 176:214-227 (2019), arXiv:1710.09351, Eq. (12):
      S(x) = log L - L exp(-(2 pi)^2 rho^2) [ 1 + (128 pi^6/3) rho^4 rho'^2 ]
which is exactly the functional this project has been using, kappa_AM = 128 pi^6/3 included. Immediately after,
they write its Euler-Lagrange equation:
      0 = rho^4 rho'' + 2 rho^3 rho'^2 - 4 pi^2 rho^5 rho'^2 + 3/(32 pi^4) rho.
(3) ITS CONSEQUENCE FOR X, WHICH IS THEIR OWN ARGUMENT. To get eta = 1/3 they balance the last two terms. That
balance is 4 pi^2 rho^5 rho'^2 = 3/(32 pi^4) rho, i.e. rho^4 rho'^2 = 3/(128 pi^6), i.e.
      X := kappa_AM rho^4 rho'^2 = (128 pi^6/3)(3/(128 pi^6)) = 1, EXACTLY.
Checked numerically: kappa_AM * 3/(128 pi^6) = 1.000000. Direct integration of their ODE from their stated
boundary condition rho(0) = 1 is stiff and blows up by x = 0.5 for every rho'(0) tried, so the balance argument
is the usable route - and it is theirs, not mine.
(4) AGAINST THIS PROJECT'S NUMBERS. Certified Gaussian states give X = 1.7165 down to 1.7018 over d = 14 to 24;
certified binomial states extrapolated in 1/n give 1.7227 at d = 12; 449's parameter-free derivation from the
UNTRUNCATED stationarity condition gives them to an rms of 0.006 %. So their local two-term equation and the
exact nonlocal one differ by a factor of 1.7071 in X.
(5) THIS IDENTIFIES THE 0.59 THAT HAS SAT IN THE RECORD SINCE 356. 1/1.7071 = 0.5858. The recurring "0.59",
recorded then as "a symptom of the wrong FORM", is exactly the ratio of the two-term LOCAL truncation to the
exact NONLOCAL answer. It was never a coefficient to be fitted; it is what truncating the functional costs.
(6) WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE IN THEIR RESULT. A constant X of ANY value gives rho proportional to
x^(1/3), so their exponent - log K ~ I^(4/3), K ~ L^(4/3) - is untouched. K goes as X^(1/6), so the prefactor
moves by 1.7071^(1/6) = 1.0932, +9.32 %. Their scaling law stands; its coefficient does not.
(7) NOVELTY, CHECKED AND LABELLED. Web searches today for a follow-up deriving the profile equation, and for the
nonlocal stationarity condition in this form, returned nothing. That is a LIMITED check - two searches and the
source paper - and it is recorded as such, not as an establishment of novelty. The one question it cannot settle
is whether Eq. (12) was ever INTENDED to hold pointwise for the optimal profile (where rho varies threefold)
rather than perturbatively about a uniform comb under their ordering (11). That is a question about the authors'
intent, and no run of mine can answer it.
(8) CONSEQUENT ACTION. A two-page note on the coefficient was written (Firdaus_2026_abbott_machta_note.pdf,
builder build_note.py).
Gates: no gate word used. (1) records that I held a belief which blocked an obvious comparison for weeks; (7)
labels the novelty check as limited rather than claiming NEW.

0.006 %.

(2) THE CHECK, RUN:
     d     states   linear X(inf)  rms      quadratic X(inf)  rms      rho(inf)   X* derived   difference
     13      18      1.718767    1.1e-04      1.720829     5.9e-06    0.63631     1.720470     -0.0209 %
     14      18      1.716869    1.1e-04      1.718925     5.1e-06    0.65191     1.718601     -0.0188 %

"THE TWO CHANNELS DO NOT AGREE" IS WITHDRAWN.
(1) THE TEST. Fit the measured X(d) against 1/n at orders 1, 2 and 3 over the eighteen certified binomial states
