## Amendment 973 (01 Oct 10:32) - PRE-REGISTERED (Tier C): the 2D bulk law with a derived curvature term; no 2D ring position beyond A = 12 has been read

1. Derivation (mine, saddle level). For capacity on the disc |x| <= A the bulk input is uniform per unit area, so the rings form a comb on
   a flat areal density, and the first-harmonic argument of 1D (BULK_C6_DERIVATION 1.1) carries over with
   I2(r) = int int psi(a) psi(b) exp(2 pi i [N(|(r + a, b)|) - N(r)]) da db, psi = N(0, 2); positional condition arg I2 = pi at each
   ring. To leading order in b, |(r + a, b)| = r + a + b^2/(2(r + a)), and the b integral is (1 + 4 pi i rho/(r + a))^(-1/2). The a
   integral sits at the complex saddle a = -i q, q = 4 pi rho (the depth saddle u = 2 i alpha of the 1D case), where the factor is
   ((r - i q)/r)^(1/2), of argument -(1/2) arctan(q/r). The 1D law PHI - arg G = pi becomes PHI - arg G + (1/2) arctan(4 pi rho/r) = pi,
   that is
       rho^2 rho' / s0 = f1(rho) - c (1/(2 pi)) arctan(4 pi rho/r),   c = 1,   r = A - d,
   with f1 the derived 1D law (933). Neglected: the variation of the b factor across the saddle's width (relative order 2/(r^2 + q^2)),
   the b^4 terms, and any change of the areal density near the wall and the centre. The sign means sparser rings than in 1D, which is
   the direction seen at A = 7-12 (970's states; a first-order estimate on those states, 0.028/0.077/0.136/0.203 against
   0.051/0.093/0.137/0.182 extra depth at A = 12, was computed before this amendment and is disclosed here).
2. Instrument q653_bulk2d_fit.py: integrates the law with two free constants (N and rho at the first fitted ring), c fixed at 0 (M0, the
   1D law), at 1 (M1, derived) or free; rings with depth >= 6 and radius >= 6. Controls run before this amendment:
   (a) the 1D capacity half-line under a fake radius A = 20, 25, 30 (true c = 0): rms M0 1.4e-6, 1.2e-6, 1.3e-6; c_fit -0.0003, 0.0000,
       0.0001; M1 is worse (4e-3 to 1.4e-2), so the curvature term is far above the instrument's floor;
   (b) data made by M1 itself (true c = 1): c_fit 1.0000 at all three.
3. Data: q650_rings2d_far.json from the continuation now running to A = 30 (q650_rings2d_far.py, a copy of q649 with its own output and
   a repaired birth step after a stop at the birth near A 17.90). States at A = 20, 25, 30; if the run stops early, the largest integer
   A >= 18 it reaches, declared before reading.

## Amendment 977 (01 Oct 10:41) - second instrument for the 2D and 3D solvers: the first births equal Dytso-Poor-Shamai's single-shell thresholds to ten digits

Source: Dytso, Poor, Shamai, "On the Capacity of the Peak Power Constrained Vector Gaussian Channel: An Estimation Theoretic
Perspective", arXiv 1804.08524v1 (downloaded to temporal_within/papers/, text extracted by me with pypdf). Their Theorem 3: the single
sphere of radius R is optimal iff R <= Rbar_n, Rbar_n the positive zero of E[(W1/|W|) h_{n/2}(R |W|)] = 1/2, W1 with density
(Q(w - R) - Q(w))/R, W2..Wn iid N(0, 1), h_v = I_v/I_{v-1} (their eq. 6). The paper prints Rbar_1 = 1.665925641 (Fig. 6 caption) and
shows Rbar_n for n up to 20 only as a plot (Fig. 2).
My evaluation of their equation (Gauss-Legendre, 400 nodes per axis, brentq): Rbar_1 = 1.665925641 (their printed value), Rbar_2 =
2.453389958, Rbar_3 = 3.065107732. My KKT solvers: 2D first birth 2.453389958 (967, d50_lib), 3D first birth 3.065107732 (976,
d70_lib3d). The two routes share no code (theirs is an estimation-theoretic identity, mine the KKT equality i(0) = i(A)).
Gates: no gate word used.

Specification (a separate extraction split the paper into spec and sealed outcome; I read only the spec): maximise -(1/2) E||X - Y||^2 - lambda I(X;Y),
lambda = 2/3, Y ~ N(0, I_2) truncated to the disc ||Y|| <= 3 (B1) or the square [-3, 3]^2 (B2); X unrestricted. The paper's
normalisation is not consistent; the spec lists four readings and argues for (a): cost per nat, beta = 1/(2 lambda) = 0.75, test-channel
variance lambda = 2/3 per coordinate. Mapping (the identity of 800): rate-distortion with slope beta = NPMLE with Gaussian kernel of sd
sigma_k = 1/sqrt(2 beta); in noise units the prior sd is 1/sigma_k and the truncation sits at 3/sigma_k.

unique; for the disc it is rotationally symmetric (rings plus possibly an origin point); for the square it is the product of the two
one-dimensional optima (separable source and distortion).

## Amendment 1011 (01 Oct 13:57) - REGISTERED (derived extension, not blind): the parity split of the centre in d dimensions is 4 (d - 1)/v^2

Derivation (mine, from 1007's 2D mechanism). Before a birth the core is the comb of zeros of J_nu with nu = d/2 - 1 (no origin mass);
before a lift-off it is the comb of J_{nu+1} plus an origin mass (nu + 1 = d/2). The McMahon pole of the core contributes
-(4 nu^2 - 1)/v^2 to 2 N(A) - K at the event (1007, phase checked on exact Bessel combs for d = 2), so
  c_birth - c_liftoff = [(4 (d/2)^2 - 1) - (4 (d/2 - 1)^2 - 1)]/v^2 = 4 (d - 1)/v^2,
which is 4/v^2 at d = 2 (1007) and 0 at d = 1 (no 1D split). The common level is not predicted.
Data (seen as e values, gaps not computed): q661 centre values with c = d - 1, K_eff from event states: d = 3 q661_d3.txt, d = 4
q661_d4.txt, d = 5 q661_d5.txt; d = 2 as 1008.
TEST: at rho_c = 0.70, 0.72, 0.74 (and wherever both event types are measured), the measured gap e_birth - e_liftoff (interpolated in
rho_c) over 4 (d - 1)/v^2 lies in 0.85-1.25 for d = 3, 4, 5 (the d = 2 ratio was 1.08-1.16). PASS if every ratio is in band; read the
trend with d. The alternatives "gap independent of d" and "gap growing like (d - 1)^2" fail the band at d = 4 and 5.

## Amendment 1027 (01 Oct 15:24) - PRE-REGISTERED: the births constant at an asymmetric meeting point (annulus), with sealed outcomes

Question. Every births test so far had a symmetric centre: the 1D interval centre, or the origin of the d-ball. An annulus
a <= |x| <= a + W has no symmetric point; its rings are born where the branch from the inner wall meets the branch from the outer
wall. Does the births law hold there, and with which constant?
Derivation (CENTRE_CONSTANT_DERIVATION 3.1-3.6 with the transverse phase of the d-dimensional bulk law). The phase condition becomes
-pi D + phi_T = pi (mod 2 pi), phi_T = ((d - 1)/2) atan(v/r), the same for both branches because the saddle always sits at +iv in the
radial direction. The far-field values of D are phi_T/pi + 1 (inner side) and phi_T/pi - 1 (outer side), and the only admissible jump
at the meeting point is still -2. The solution is eta = eta_sym - (phi_T/pi) xi^2: the extra term changes only the far-field slopes
(the inner branch obeys rho^2 rho_z/s0 = f1 + ((d - 1)/(2 pi)) atan(4 pi rho/r), the outer branch the same with a minus sign), and
it leaves the +-1/12 offsets of eta_sym unchanged. Matching gives N_in(x0 - a) + N_out(a + W - x0) = K + 1/6 at the sharp point,
x0 where the two branch densities are equal. Prediction: annulus births carry the 1D constant 1/6 + delta(rho_c), with no Gouy term
(the ball's (d - 1)/2 comes from the focus at the origin, which the annulus does not have).
Instruments. q686_annulus_births.py (d85 library; continuation in W from 2 to 36 at fixed a, births bisected to 1e-7, outcomes
written only to q686_annulus_a{a}_d2_SEALED.json; runs a = 20 and a = 10 started 15:22). q687_annulus_centre.py: two-branch
readout (each branch fitted with its signed law, two constants, atoms with depth >= 6 and >= 6 from the midpoint; e = N_in + N_out - K
at rho_in = rho_out). Control: on the 13 certified 1D states c60_small_K26-38 it returns q661's e to every printed digit
(0.16003 ... 0.16262). Matched comparator: the same readout on the d = 1 chain (q684 DIM 1, run extended to half-width 19), which

same count K before the event. FAIL otherwise; the number of events in and out of the band is reported. Reported for contrast, no

## Amendment 1040 (01 Oct 16:41) - PRE-REGISTERED (p_c runs unread): the whole-curve wall is special to the circle; every superellipse with p > 2 has a broken wall

Reasoning (heuristic, label: not derived). On the wall the KKT function has a non-zero outward derivative (the wall is a hard
constraint; about +0.3 at A = 3 from the shell states, 1026). If the boundary moves outward by eps(theta), D on the wall changes by
d_n D eps(theta), a term that keeps every angular mode of the shape. The only terms that can cancel it come from changing the masses,
and they pass through the Gaussian kernel twice (p = phi * mu, D = -phi * log p), so their angular modes decay like exp(-c m^2).
A superellipse's boundary has Fourier coefficients that decay polynomially (non-even p: |x|^p is not analytic at the edge midpoints)
or exponentially (even p, an algebraic curve), so its high modes cannot be cancelled and D cannot be constant along the whole
curve. If this holds, the circle's continuous wall is a consequence of its symmetry, the break point is p_c = 2, and the first
gaps sit where the boundary is least smooth (the edge midpoints for non-even p).
Predictions on the runs q698_p{2.1,2.2,2.3,2.4}_A3 (from uniform, stopping at a bracket of 2e-5; started 16:35, outputs unread):
(1) every one of them has a broken wall: some wall point with D below its maximum by more than 5 brackets and wall density below
1e-3 of its peak; (2) the deepest wall gap of each run includes the edge midpoint (bin 0). Falsifier: a run at p = 2.1 or 2.2 whose
wall D stays within 1 bracket of its maximum all around the curve.
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 1052 (01 Oct 17:40) - sealed runs resumed with q686i to W = 44; a derived reason for the wall break at non-analytic points

(1) q686i validated on the unsealed a = 12: birth 3.3173869, split 5.797929, birth 8.0106515, split 10.081221, identical to q686f,
in 170 s against 255 s. The three q686f sealed runs were stopped at 17:39:31, their files copied unread (*_beforeresume.json), and
resumed with q686i from their own last saved states (RESUME=1, read by the script only) at 17:39:33, WMAX 44 as registered in 1050.
(2) WALL_ANALYTICITY_NOTE.md. D is real-analytic on the plane (a Gaussian convolution of log p, entire). On a supported wall arc
D = C, and where the outward slope is non-zero (0.448 for the disk at A = 3; positive by continuity on the nearby shapes) the
implicit function theorem makes {D = C} a real-analytic curve containing that arc. So a supported wall arc with non-zero slope is
real-analytic, and a boundary point where the boundary is not real-analytic (the superellipse's edge midpoints for non-even p,
however close p is to 2) cannot lie inside a supported arc. This accounts for 1040/1047 (gaps at the midpoints from p = 2.1) and is
silent on analytic shapes, which keep the whole wall when close to the circle (1041, 1045); even p = 4 breaks by a separate mechanism
(positivity of the wall density). Counting unknowns explains why a free interior ring survives (position and density for D = C and
zero slope) while the fixed wall does not. Checks it predicts: p = 2.05 and 2.02 have the midpoint outside the interior of the
supported wall; supported wall points have positive outward slope on every broken superellipse.
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 1054 (01 Oct 17:45) - literature gate for the 2D wall findings: a published theorem on ellipses; the "whole wall" readings of 1044 and 1048 are qualified

Searches (four, logged with this entry): support topology of capacity-achieving inputs on non-circular 2D sets; rate-distortion
of a uniform source on a square or polygon; deterministic annealing on 2D uniform sources; support on analytic curves for arbitrary
compact sets. Read in extracted text: Dytso, Barletta, Kramer, arXiv 2401.17084 (papers/bridge_cap2d3d/extract/arxiv_2401.17084v1_c.txt
and papers/litgate_2dwall/), and Fahs, Abou-Faycal 1602.00878 (downloaded, papers/litgate_2dwall/, not yet read in full).
Found. 2401.17084 studies exactly the ellipse (the 2 x 2 MIMO channel with a peak constraint reduces to an input inside an ellipse with
axes rp >= rm). Their Theorem 3 (lines 325-329): for 0 <= rm <= rp < sqrt(2), "supp(PX*) is a finite set for rm != rp", and the input is
uniform on the circle for rm = rp. Their proof: an infinite support on the ellipse would, by the identity theorem, make the KKT relation
hold on the whole ellipse; continued to the imaginary axis it contradicts a growth bound. They state as open (lines 611-615) "the rate
at which the cardinality of the set supp(PX*) approaches infinity as rm -> rp".
Consequences for the record. (1) For small ellipses the wall support of a non-circular ellipse is finite, a set of isolated points.
My ellipse runs (A = 3, 1041/1044; A = 4, 1048) are outside their size range, but a near-circular ellipse has a finite support whose
cardinality grows as rm -> rp, so the "whole wall" read there (density 0.96-1.00 of its peak, D within 1.8 brackets) can be a dense
finite set whose gaps are below the bracket. 1044 is qualified: no gap is visible at a bracket of 2e-5; whether the wall is whole is
not established. The same holds for the rose (1045 (1), passed as registered; its "whole wall" reading is qualified). (2) The superellipse
gaps at the non-analytic midpoints (1040, 1047) are deep (tens of brackets) and stand; WALL_ANALYTICITY_NOTE Step 3 stands, and its line
"analytic shapes carry no such obstruction" must read "carry no obstruction from Step 3"; 2401.17084 gives a different obstruction for
small ellipses. (3) Novelty words: none. The topology change on superellipses and the non-analytic-point mechanism were not found in
the sources read; the discreteness of the ellipse wall at small size is published (2401.17084).
Gates: "not found" used with its source list; no novelty word.

## Amendment 1068 (01 Oct 19:08) - the ripple of a regular K-gon on the circle in closed form, checked; the 12-atom structures violate KKT near the circle at 80 nodes

(1) DERIVED (first order in the mode amplitude). For K equal atoms at radius r and angles theta0 + 2 pi j/K, the Jacobi-Anger
expansion keeps only angular modes that are multiples of K: p(y) = phi(s) e^(-r^2/2) [I_0(rs) + 2 I_K(rs) cos(K(psi - theta0)) + ...] at
y = s(cos psi, sin psi). Then on the circle D(alpha) = D_0 - 2 R_K cos(K(alpha - theta0)) + ..., with
    R_K(r) = 2 int_0^inf s exp(-(s^2 + r^2)/2) I_K(rs)^2 / I_0(rs) ds,
so the K-gon violates KKT midway between atoms by 2 R_K. At r = 1.3 (mpmath, 40 digits): 2 R_K = 1.96e-4 (K 6), 1.44e-6 (8), 6.91e-9
(10), 2.3437e-11 (12), 1.17e-16 (16), 2.38e-22 (20), 2.36e-28 (24). Checked: the measured violation of 12 equal atoms on the circle at 80
nodes is +2.344e-11 (1066), equal to 2 R_12 to the printed digits; for 16 atoms the measured +3.2e-15 is the D error floor and 2 R_16
lies below it. For large K, 2 R_K behaves like (r^2/2)^K/K! up to slowly varying factors, which is the heuristic of 1060 (c).
(2) 80 nodes, structures with the X orbit (Theorem 4): X + Y + 2G (K = 12) gives I equal to the rotated 12-atom I to 1e-13 and

## Amendment 1078 (01 Oct 19:54) - the near-circle perturbation series for the ellipse density diverges like (m^3 eps)^(m/2); PRE-REGISTERED: its sign and order pattern in the saved 16-atom solutions

Derivation (q715_chain.py, definitions and quadrature only). Write the optimal input on the ellipse as a density f = 1 + sum a_m cos(m theta)
in the polar angle, boundary radius rho(theta) = r - eps sin^2(theta). D = C on the whole boundary, expanded in eps, gives at harmonic
m + 2 the balance -J_(m+2) a_(m+2) - (eps/4)[d2 J_m + d1 J_(m+2)] a_m + ... = 0, where -J_m(r1, r2) is the response of D at radius r2 to a
density harmonic m on radius r1 (q715 docstring), so a_(m+2)/a_m = -q_m eps with q_m = [d2 J_m + d1 J_(m+2)]/(4 J_(m+2)). At r = 1.3:
q_4 = 56.75, q_6 = 151.1, q_8 = 311.6, q_10 = 553.9, q_12 = 893.5, q_14 = 1345.6, q_16 = 1925.0; check 4 J_12 = 2.3437e-11 and 4 J_16 =
1.1694e-16 (the ripple of 1068). For large m, J_m/J_(m+2) grows like m^2 and d J_m/J_m like m/r, so q_m grows like m^3: the formal
series has a_(2n) ~ (-1)^n eps^n prod q, which shrinks while q_m eps < 1 and then grows without bound. The term turns at m*(eps) with
q_(m*) eps = 1: m* about 6 at eps = 0.01, 14 at 1e-3, about 130 at 1e-6 (q_m extrapolated as m^3), so m* grows like eps^(-1/3). This is
the mechanism behind the finite support (no positive density solves D = C) and it suggests a count of order eps^(-1/3), a power law,
against the K log K ~ log(1/eps) guess in DBK_CARDINALITY_NOTE. The rule that turns m* into a count is not derived; the terms left out
(products of harmonics, the background change at harmonic 2) are smaller by about 1/m^3 for large m and are not small at m = 2 or 4.
Status: DERIVED at leading order, heuristic for the count.

PRE-REGISTERED test on the saved K = 16 solutions (q708_rp1.3_rm1.29_X1Y1G3.json, eps = 0.01; q708_rp1.3_rm1.299_X1Y1G3.json, eps =

(b) Order in eps: a_4 falls by a factor in [70, 130] and a_6 by a factor in [700, 1300] from eps = 0.01 to 1e-3 (leading orders eps^2 and

## Amendment 1109 (02 Oct 02:22) - correction to the reading of 1108: the optimum cannot jump

The capacity-achieving input is unique (mutual information is strictly concave in the input law for this channel), and the input set,
the ellipse, moves continuously with rm. By the maximum theorem the optimal input is then weakly continuous in rm. A new support point
must therefore enter with mass tending to zero at the event, and no existing atom can move or change mass by a finite amount there. The
"subcritical birth, then a jump" reading of 1108 cannot describe the optimum. Either the held-mass solutions on the larger-eps side
(not converged, 1e-12) are not the optimal branch, or the zero-mass entry at the 14 -> 16 event comes with a continuous change that my
trials did not seed (a pair born at 90 deg with a separation growing from zero, as at a degenerate touch). The event itself (KKT lost at
eps = 0.163205, 1103 part 1) stands. Next: held-mass solves at 160 bits with difference step 1e-14 and up to 80 Newton steps (started
02:22) to see whether the backward trend survives convergence.
Gates: no gate word used.

Both trackers reach rm = 1.2 (eps 0.1) with K = 8 and strongly negative margins: P 1.98, X + Y + G(46.32 deg), midpoint margins -3.2e-4 and
-2.8e-4; P 2.02, 2G (25.27, 66.11 deg), margins -9.4e-5 and -4.5e-4. On the ellipse the count goes from 6 to at least 18 over the same eps.
1136 (c) asked for each event within 10 % of the ellipse's eps at equal K: there is no K = 10 event near 0.2394: FAIL. (a) and (b) have no
event to score: VOID.
Reading. A superellipse with fixed P != 2 does not tend to the circle as eps -> 0; it tends to a squircle, whose optimal input at this size
is a finite D4-symmetric set (eight atoms here), so its count stays bounded. The growth of the count is a property of families that tend
to the circle, where the uniform law is the limit; the ellipse is one such family (a pure two-fold term). A proper third case is a family
r(theta) = R(1 + eps cos 4 theta) (four-fold, tending to the circle), where the flattest points are at 45 deg and births should come there.
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 1148 (02 Oct 05:07) - 1146 PASSES; the first event of every n-fold family is set by circle data alone: depth = 2 R_n(rp)/g(rp)

(1) The n bump atoms sit on the circle r = rp for every dent depth delta, with masses 1/n by symmetry, so the n-atom state is the regular
n-gon of the circle and does not change with delta; only the points where KKT is checked move inward, by u = delta (1 - cos n t)/2.
Expanding D of the n-gon about r = rp: D - C = R_n (1 - cos n t) - g u + (higher harmonics, R_n u, u^2), so to first order
D - C = (R_n - g delta/2)(1 - cos n t). It vanishes at every t at once when delta = 2 R_n/g, where 2 R_n is the circle ripple of the
n-gon and g = dD/dr at r = rp is the radial slope of the KKT function of the uniform input on the circle.
(2) q750 (1D Rician integral for the uniform circle input): g(1.3) = 0.669971388, 1/g = 1.492601053492; g(1.2) = 0.672115137,
g(1.4) = 0.662104828.
(3) q751 (the n-gon at rp = 1.3, D in ball arithmetic, 150 nodes; for each t the delta where D - C = 0, extrapolated to the bump in t^2):

proof uses zero counting of an analytic KKT function, and the KKT function along an ellipse is analytic in t. No novelty claim.

## Amendment 1157 (02 Oct 05:43) - BACKLOG 27: which steps of the Barletta-Dytso locality proof carry to the ellipse (ELLIPSE_LOCALITY_NOTE.md)

Read from the extracted text of arXiv 2609.10039: Lemmas 1-7, Proposition 1, Theorem 2, Corollary 1, Propositions 2-3, Theorem 3.
Carries to the ellipse boundary z(t): the KKT conditions, the entire extension in t, the local zero types (even multiplicity on a
closed curve, as their Remark 2 says these need only the KKT inequality and analyticity), weak continuity in rm, Hurwitz, and the
persistence of every nondegenerate support point (their Proposition 3 with the tangential second derivative). So on the ellipse a count
change can happen only at a degenerate support point or an inactive contact point. First failing step: Lemma 7, the global zero count
N_mul <= 2K, which rests on Karlin's oscillation theorem and the zero bound for exponential polynomials, both one-dimensional; along the
ellipse g is a 2D Gaussian transform restricted to a curve and f_Y(z(t)) is a sum of exponentials of trigonometric polynomials.
Replacement needed: a zero count 2K + s with 4 <= s < 8 (a vertex-orbit event already costs 4 units, a generic orbit 8), plus a step
excluding the major vertex. The trackers' confinement of every event to the minor vertex (four sizes, plus rp 1.0) is the empirical
side of that missing count.
Gates: no gate word used.

2.6e-3, at large r), while the 42 steps across an event do not (median 1e-16, max 1.4e-4). Cause: in the LFP the edge atoms carry the
smallest masses (w at +-m: 0.00476 at m 18.65, 0.00059 at 40.9) and the central ones the largest (0.056 to 0.023); at fixed K the edge
mass shrinks, so S_(K-1) = 1 - (edge mass) rises. In capacity the edge carries the largest masses (the ellipse X atoms: 0.29 per atom at
rp 1.0) and they fall, which is the direction majorization needs; that matches 1155 and Barletta and Dytso's Fig. 5.
Reading for the target: majorization is a property of the capacity problem tied to where its largest masses sit, not a shared law of
the three count-law problems; the LFP's evolution between events runs the other way at its edge.

recorded with the K_c values if H1 holds.

## Amendment 1187 (02 Oct 07:26) - BACKLOG 29 closed: kappa_n derived from circle quantities; the two-stage n-fold law has no free constant

Derivation (q760). Treat the regular 2n-ring at radius r with angular density f = (1/2 pi)(1 + b_n cos n theta + ...) and output density
p = p0 (1 + h), h = sum b_m q_m(rho) cos m phi, q_m = I_m(r rho)/I_0(r rho). Along the curve s(t) = r + v(t), v = (delta/2) cos n t
(relative to the ring's radius, the ring at the mean radius):
    D = D0(s) - b_n J_n(s) cos n t + (ring ripple, 4 J_2n at the midpoints = 2 R_2n) + (1/4) b_n^2 L_n(s) cos 2n t + ...,
    J_m(s) = int rho e^{-(rho^2+s^2)/2} I_m(s rho) q_m(rho) d rho,   L_n(s) = int rho e^{-(rho^2+s^2)/2} q_n(rho)^2 I_2n(s rho) d rho.
The pairs' shift toward the bumps sets b_n = -2 sin(n alpha) so that the harmonic-n term cancels: b_n = g delta/(2 J_n). Collecting the
harmonic-2n terms of second order (the radial curvature g2 v^2/2, the cross term -b_n J_n' v cos n t, and the quadratic b_n^2 L_n/4),
the midpoint margin is 2 R_2n - kappa_n delta^2 with
    kappa_n = g J_n'/(4 J_n) - g2/8 - g^2 L_n/(8 J_n^2),
g = D0'(r), g2 = D0''(r), J_n' = dJ_n/ds at s = r; every factor is a circle integral.
Values at r = 1.3 (g 0.669971388, g2 0.6136746): kappa_n = 0.648633 (n 6), 0.911403 (8), 1.172615 (10), 1.432889 (12); measured from

term g J_n'/(4 J_n) carries the factor n (J_n'/J_n = 4.39, 5.94, 7.48, 9.03), which is the near-linear law of 1184.

## Amendment 1213 (02 Oct 08:53) - PRE-REGISTERED: the missing source term in b_2

1191 set b_2 = g eps/(2 J_2) by cancelling the shape term g (eps/2) cos 2t against the density response b_2 J_2 cos 2t, as in the n-fold
derivation (1187) where the ring sat on one circle. On the ellipse the atoms themselves sit at radius R + (eps/2) cos 2t, so the source
ring is displaced as well, and its displacement has its own harmonic-2 response H_2 (the response of D at radius s to a source ring at
radius r displaced by cos 2 theta): H_2(s) = int rho e^{-(rho^2+s^2)/2} I_2(s rho) [rho I_2'(r rho) - r I_2(r rho)]/I_0(r rho) d rho, at
s = r = R. The first-order balance becomes b_2^src = eps (g - H_2)/(2 J_2). PRE-REGISTERED (no H_2 computed yet): H_2/g lies near 0.5 at
the event radii, so that (a) K b_2^src is constant over the 22 events to 2 % at a value between 3.5 and 4.3, and (b) at the three rp 1.3
births it is within 6 % of the rings' carried modulation K beta* = 4.09, 3.78, 3.70 (1211). Fails if (a) or (b) fails.
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 1224 (02 Oct 09:34) - a new instrument, the extremal sector of the smooth density from circle integrals; PRE-REGISTERED: its control, the large-order growth, and an event rule

Instrument (q764_extremal_series.py). Write the ellipse as z(t) = R e^{it} + eta e^{-it}, R = (rp + rm)/2, eta = eps/2, and the input
density in t as 1 + sum_k c_2k cos 2kt. Rotating the curve with t multiplies eta by e^{2i alpha}, so harmonic 2k first appears at order
eta^k, and the terms conj(eta)^k e^{2ikt} form a closed sector (set z = R e^{it}, conj(z) = R e^{-it} + eta e^{it}). In it the output
density is P_0(rho)(1 + sum Q_k w^k), w = eta e^{2i psi}, the log is a power series in w, and D along the curve has coefficients d_k
that are radial integrals of Bessel products; KKT (d_k = 0) gives a_k = d_k(a_k = 0)/J_2k(R) order by order, and c_2k = 2 a_k (eps/2)^k
at leading order. At first order this is exactly 1214: a_1 = (g - H_2)/(2 J_2) - 1/R. No 2D quadrature, no Newton, no soft modes.
Seen before this registration: a smoke run at R = 1.2184, N = 3 (a_1 1.457996, a_2 18.6636, a_3 212.734).
PRE-REGISTERED:
(C) Control: a_1 at R = 1.15675, 1.19638, 1.2184 equals 1214's beta_t/eps from its printed K beta_t (1.8194, 1.5763, 1.4591) within
0.3 % (the rounding of three printed digits); and a_30 at R = 1.2 agrees to 8 digits between 192 and 384 nodes and between RM 26 and 32.
(G) Growth: the ratios r_k = a_(k+1)/a_k for k up to at least 30 at R = 1.0, 1.2, 1.3. If r_k/k changes by less than 3 % over the last
ten computed steps, the reading is a factorial power 1 and, with the event rule below, a count K ~ const/eps; if r_k/k^(3/2) does,
power 3/2 and K ~ eps^(-2/3). Any other behaviour is reported as such.
(E) Event rule (the comb rule of 1082-1083, BACKLOG 19, in the t parametrisation): the K-ring is lost when the formal harmonic-K
coefficient falls to the comb's amplitude, |c_K(eps)| = 2 |a_(K/2)(R)| (eps/2)^(K/2) = alpha with R = rp - eps/2. Two index choices,
both scored: E_b with K = K before the event, E_a with K = K after. For each of the 26 events (rp 0.8-1.4, K after 8-18; table in
q761 plus 1193, 1216, 1219, 1222, 1223) solve the rule for eps and compare with the observed eps. E_b or E_a PASSES (shape) if
eps_obs/eps_rule is constant over the 26 events within +- 3 % with one fitted alpha; PASSES (parameter-free) if within +- 3 % of 1 at
alpha = 2. Expectation stated now: the shape test is the informative one; the extremal sector drops terms of relative order
eta conj(eta) times growth factors, which at eps 0.1-0.34 need not be small, so a level offset is likely and a trend with eps would
measure those terms.
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 1232 (02 Oct 09:59) - one comb rule for the n-fold family too? PRE-REGISTERED: its orders 1-3 against the measured n-fold events

Observation (algebra, no new number). The n-fold stage laws are the comb rule at orders 1 and 2: at first order the formal density's
harmonic n is c_n = delta g/(2 J_n), and c_n = 2 is delta_1 = 4 J_n/g = 2 R_n/g (1148); at second order the uncancelled harmonic-2n
forcing kappa_n delta^2 equals 2 J_2n c_2n, so 2 R_2n = kappa_n delta^2 is c_2n = 2 (1187). Both formulas drop terms of relative order
n delta and J_n: at n = 4 the stage-1 ratio is 1.5286 against 1/g = 1.4926 (+2.4 %, 1148), and q760 now gives kappa_4 = 0.383192, so
delta_2 = sqrt(2 R_8/kappa_4) = 1.9396e-3 against the measured 1.921e-3 (-1.0 %, 1141).
Instrument to build (q770): the extremal sector of the n-fold curve. With z = R e^{it} + s (e^{i(n+1)t} + e^{-i(n-1)t}), s = delta/4,
R = rp - delta/2, the terms of charge +n close as for the ellipse; the kernel factor is exp(s e^{int}(rho cos u - R) - s^2 e^{2int}/2)
= sum_j (s e^{int})^j He_j(rho cos u - R)/j!, and the density coefficients a_k of harmonic nk follow order by order from radial
integrals. Comb rule: the ring of K = nk atoms is lost when 2 a_k(R) s^k = 2.
PRE-REGISTERED (no q770 output yet; the measured values below are in the record, so this is a parameter-free check, not a blind one):
rp 1.3, four-fold: k = 1 against 0.023818 and k = 2 against 0.001921, each within +-0.5 % (where the leading formulas miss by 2.4 and
1.0 %); k = 3 against the third event 0.000368 (the event beside each axis at 13.5 deg, 1143) within +-3 %. Six-fold: k = 1 against
2.9346e-4 and k = 2 against 6.01e-6, within +-0.5 %. n = 8, 10, 12: k = 1 and 2 against 1146/1187 (2.1518e-6, 1.03147e-8,
3.4982e-11; 1.1325e-8, 1.424e-11, 1.2823e-14) within +-0.3 %. A failure at n = 4 with passes at n >= 6 would mean the comb rule holds
only where the leading formulas already do.

the question that decides the ellipse's asymptotic count (rings of 26-48 atoms).

## Amendment 1259 (02 Oct 11:53) - curve versus filled region; an observation about the proof of Theorem 4 of 2401.17084 (UNCHECKED against later versions)

(1) Framing. Every solve in this record constrains the input to the curve (KKT checked along it). Dytso, Barletta and Kramer's problem
(arXiv 2401.17084, text extracted to papers/bridge_cap2d3d/extract/arxiv_2401.17084v1.txt) constrains it to the filled ellipse E, with
KKT (4): D <= C on E, and (5): D = C on the support; for rp <= sqrt 2 their Theorem 3 puts the support on the boundary, so on the
ellipse the two problems have the same optimum. For other curves they need not.
(2) q782 (interior check, D by q719's rule copied as text): the polar two-fold optimum at rp 0.8, delta 0.10 (one G orbit at 30.41 deg, no
atom at (0.8, 0)) has D - C <= -2.18e-3 at all 210 interior points of a 14 x 14 polar grid of the quadrant (largest at 32.1 deg, fraction
0.995 of the boundary radius, next to the atom) and <= -4.3e-3 at 42 points on rays 0-90 deg; with (5) at its four atoms (residual
5e-33) and the curve scan of 1236, it satisfies (4)-(5) for the filled region bounded by this curve, so it is that region's optimum too
(the KKT conditions are sufficient). The farthest point of the region, (0.8, 0), carries no atom.
(3) The proof of Theorem 4 in the extracted v1 text (Section III-C) uses Lemma 7 (if Pr(X1 > t) = 0 then dD/dx1 > 0 for x1 > t, by
Tweedie's formula) and states that (53), D(x1, x2) > D(t, x2) for x1 > t, "would violate the KKT condition (4)". Lemma 7 uses nothing
specific to the ellipse, and the region of (2) is a filled, doubly symmetric region whose farthest point is unique, so the argument
as written would place (0.8, 0) in that region's support, which (2) contradicts. Where the step needs more: (53) gives D > C only at
points (x1, x2) with x1 > t whose height x2 is that of a support point with first coordinate t; those support points lie on the
boundary away from the axis, and points to their right at the same height are outside the region. Reading: the statement of
Theorem 4 for the ellipse agrees with every ellipse optimum computed in this record (the major-vertex atoms are always present), and
the step from (53) to a violation of (4) needs an ingredient specific to the ellipse that the v1 text does not state.
UNCHECKED: whether a later version or the published paper adds that ingredient; to be searched and read before this is used anywhere.
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 1279 (02 Oct 14:20) - literature gate, BACKLOG 30 and the comb rule: four more sources read from extracted text, nothing bears on it

Read from text I extracted myself (temporal_within/papers/litgate_comb/):
- Huleihel, Goldfeld, Koch, Madiman, Medard, ISIT 2018 (UC3M e-archivo PDF): the circle-uniform input with its phase quantized; a
  sufficient number of phase points for a small capacity backoff, and allocation of points across amplitude circles. The constraint
  region stays a disc; no curve other than the circle, no KKT ripple, no Bessel terms.
- Bernardo, Zhu, Evans, arXiv 2106.11007: phase quantization at the output; the optimum is a rotated 2^b-PSK. Output-side, not a
  perturbed input constraint.
- Favano, Ferrari, Magarini, Barletta, arXiv 2101.08643: norm-bounded MIMO; concentric spheres, a lower bound on their number and an
  iterative algorithm. Rotation-invariant region only.
- Favano et al., arXiv 2111.13179: sphere-packing upper bound for an arbitrary convex amplitude region (Minkowski sums, intrinsic
  volumes of ellipsoids). A capacity bound only; nothing about the support.
- Chan, Hranilovic, Kschischang, IEEE T-IT 51(6) 2005: the support is sparse for bounded inputs, concentric shells when the region is
  a ball. No statement about atom counts on a curve.
Not readable: Favano's PhD thesis (politesi.polimi.it) answers with a Cloudflare challenge; not bypassed. Its papers above are the
published parts I could reach.
Verdict for BACKLOG 30 and the comb rule: none of these treats a peak region that departs from the circle, the ripple of the KKT
function, or a count change of the ring. The gate stays partial (thesis unread; ISIT 2024 version of 2401.17084 behind
authentication).
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 1280 (02 Oct 14:36) - PRE-REGISTERED, blind: a bridge test of the comb rule on a second problem, the least favourable prior for a normal mean on the ellipse

Bigger fact under test. The comb rule (1224-1249) says a K-ring is lost when the formal smooth density's harmonic K reaches what the
ring itself supplies (2, the Dirac comb's amplitude). Only the coefficients a_k belong to the problem; the threshold belongs to the
comb. If that is right, the rule must hold with the same threshold for any problem whose KKT function makes a ring on the ellipse,
with that problem's own a_k. Second problem: X ~ N(theta, I_2) with theta known to lie on the ellipse (rp, rm), squared-error loss;
the least favourable prior (LFP) maximises the Bayes risk, and its KKT function is the risk of the posterior mean,
r(theta) = E|delta(theta + Z) - theta|^2 <= B on the curve, = B on the support. On the circle the uniform prior is least favourable by
rotation invariance, as uniform input is capacity-achieving there.

Instrument (validated before any LFP solve):
- q784_sector_numeric.py (sha256 d11120f6...): the extremal sector of q764 computed by direct numerical evaluation of a KKT function at
  complexified positions (z = R e^{it}, zb = R e^{-it} + eta e^{it}), with the harmonic-2k coefficient fixed to zero order by order.
  Rotation covariance makes that coefficient linear in A_k = a_k eta^k with an eta-free slope, so any small eta gives the same a_k.
  Check against the independent radial-Bessel derivation q764 at R 1.0 (capacity): equal in all 16 printed digits for k = 1-12
  (a_1 3.213278432580704 ... a_12 7.938425591861421e18). Plane quadrature 96 x 96 nodes, 256 bits; Gaussian normalisation error 5e-61.
- LFP at R 1.0: a_1 0.2969015011651190, a_2 13.75739989123640, a_3 155.9086819202327, a_4 2324.488202624800, a_5 42661.22944911021,
  a_6 974475.1771242425, a_7 26218757.32973813, a_8 846664098.5120159, ..., a_12 3.217382781906479e15, all positive; identical in every
  printed digit at eta 0.01 and 0.005 (q784/lfp_R1.0_eta*.log). They differ from the capacity values (a_4 29645, a_8 1.39e11): the
  LFP needs its harmonics less, so its rings change at larger eps.
- q786_lfp_wallchain.py (sha256 a77e5556...): copy of q719 with the Bayes risk and its score-form gradient on the separable
  Gauss-Hermite rule. Check: two-atom prior at +-0.8 on the x axis, where the posterior mean is 0.8 tanh(0.8 x): risk at (0.8, 0) equals

## Amendment 1283 (02 Oct 14:56) - why the bridge failed: capacity rings follow the smooth density below harmonic K to six digits, least-favourable-prior rings do not

Three checks, each able to fail, run after 1282:
1. The ring side of the rule is the same for both problems. Regular K-ring on the circle R 0.93 (q719 / q786 KKT functions, 200
   nodes): KKT value at a midpoint minus at an atom, against the linear response 4 |slope_(K/2)| from q784 at R 0.93:
   capacity K 6 8.0590e-6 vs 8.0583e-6, K 8 1.8397e-8 vs 1.8397e-8, K 12 2.7571e-14 vs 2.7571e-14; LFP K 6 8.0079e-5 vs 8.0067e-5,
   K 8 2.4821e-7 vs 2.4821e-7, K 12 5.7152e-13 vs 5.7152e-13. Linear response holds for the comb in both problems.
2. The shape side is not the cause either. q790_full_numeric.py (new, sha256 b7eae924...; the full formal density on the real ellipse, all orders in
   eps, Newton on its cosine coefficients until the KKT harmonics are below 1e-40): LFP at rp 1.0, eps 0.143045: c_2 0.10256,
   c_4 0.21652, c_6 0.21451, c_8 0.28280, c_10 0.45654; c_6 agrees with the extremal value 0.2135 of 1282 within 0.5 %.
3. The premise of the rule fails for the LFP. Ring harmonics b_j = 2 sum m cos(j t) of the pre-event state against the full c_j:
   - capacity rp 1.3, K 10 at eps 0.207240: b 0.331127, 0.451148, 0.561937, 0.914573 (j 2-8) vs c 0.331126, 0.451144, 0.561959,
     0.916714; j = 10: b 1.74795, c 1.88080.
   - capacity rp 1.3, K 12 at eps 0.182742: b 0.278672, 0.330040, 0.352378, 0.491135, 0.858484 (j 2-10) vs c 0.278671, 0.330038,
     0.352374, 0.491137, 0.859105; j = 12: b 1.75566, c 1.78872.
   - LFP rp 1.0, K 6 at eps 0.143045: b_2 0.0350 vs c_2 0.1026; b_4 0.8815 vs c_4 0.2165; b_6 1.6353 vs c_6 0.2145.
   - LFP rp 1.0, K 8 at eps 0.08375 (valid ring, G 54.81 deg, masses 0.18108 / 0.11707 / 0.10093): b 2-8 -0.0151, 0.5673,
     0.9471, 1.3538 vs c 0.0438, 0.0617, 0.0328, 0.0230.
Reading. The comb rule assumes that a ring copies the smooth density at every harmonic below its own and differs only by its comb.
Capacity rings do so to five or six digits right up to the event; the rule then follows from linear response (check 1), which is
why it held within 2 % there. LFP rings break that premise by factors of 3 to 10 at low harmonics: they are irregular rings whose
KKT function is shaped by low harmonics into a nonpositive function vanishing at the atoms, far from the uniform state. Their count
grows much more slowly (K 8 from eps 0.143 to at least 0.064 at rp 1.0; the registered rule with the LFP a_k gives K 16 already at 0.127).
Consequence for the HIGHEST TARGET: on near-circular curves the count law is not shared by capacity and the LFP, unlike the 1D
count law. The comb rule's domain is now stated by a measurable test (b_j = c_j for j < K), not by the problem's name.
Open: what decides which regime a problem is in (candidate: the size of the shape forcing at low harmonics against the comb's
freedom), and whether LFP rings enter the copying regime as K grows. Next cheap test: the NPMLE / rate-distortion problem (q789) at
the source width where its a_k are largest (s 0.5), where the rule would predict events at the MAJOR vertex.
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 1285 (02 Oct 15:01) - PRE-REGISTERED, blind: the comb rule on a third problem, the NPMLE / rate-distortion dual with centres on the ellipse, at the source width where its a_k alternate

Problem: the population N(0, s^2 I) with s = 0.5 is fitted by a mixture of unit-variance Gaussians whose centres lie on the ellipse
(rp 1.0, rm = 1 - eps); maximise int log f_G dP (the NPMLE; by Yang 2310.18908 and Rose 1994 the dual of rate-distortion). KKT:
E_Y[phi(Y - theta)/p(Y)] <= 1 on the curve, = 1 on the support. On the circle the uniform mixing measure is optimal by symmetry.
Why this case. Its extremal a_k (q784, eta-free) alternate in sign at R 1.0: -76.23, 10230.9, -2327844, 7.567e8, -3.336e11, 1.793e14,
-1.132e17, 7.674e19, ... (s 0.5; q784/rd_R1.0_sscan.txt), so (-1)^k a_k > 0 for every k computed: the smooth density's harmonics all
peak at the MINOR vertex. The rule then says the minor-vertex atom is anchored and every count change happens at the MAJOR vertex,
the opposite of the capacity and LFP ellipses; with K = 2 mod 4 there is no major-vertex atom (X birth there), with K = 0 mod 4 there
is one (X split there). The magnitudes are 24 (k 1) to 25 000 (k 4) times the capacity values at the same R: strong shape forcing. Whether
strong forcing goes with the copying regime of 1283 is open; this case tests it. A pass supports 'the rule holds wherever rings copy
the smooth density, whatever the problem'; a fail of place would mean the sign rule itself does not carry.
Seen before registering (states above every scored event, recorded so): at eps 0.05 the X + Y guess gave a negative X mass, and the
two-atom Y structure is KKT-valid (scan maximum 0 at the atom, rd05/s0, s1).
Registered predictions (q785 from q784 rd at 256 bits, SRC_S 0.5, rule 2 |a_(K/2)| (eps/2)^(K/2) = 2 with R = rp - eps/2):

## Amendment 1310 (02 Oct 17:36) - copying rings satisfy the KKT equations to 1e-11 before any solve; why Newton then stalls; the K 12 kind of s 2 left unresolved so far

Diagnostic solves (q786 / q789 at 110 bits, NGH 200) started from q796 copying rings:

The same rings at 160 bits behave alike. So the ring built only from the smooth density's harmonics 2..K-2 already satisfies D = C at
every orbit and zero tangential derivative at every G atom to about 1e-11, away from any event as well as at events (1289-1308):
the copying premise holds along the whole branch, at intermediate eps as at the event.
Newton then stalls (residual flat near those values for 20-30 iterations): what is left lies in the direction that changes the
ring's own harmonic K, which costs only the response at harmonic K (slope of order 1e-13 here), so the Jacobian is nearly singular
there and the damped step cannot use it. Continuation from converged neighbours does not have this problem; the trackers resume that
way (LFP from the last converged state of lfp10/t6, eps 0.172; NPMLE s 2 through held split angles 86-78 deg, rd2/sp12b).
NPMLE s 2 K 12 kind (registered Y split at the minor vertex): direct split trials and the held angle 88.5 deg crept (1.7e-9); still
unresolved; the value test of 1308 stands.

## Amendment 1311 (02 Oct 17:50) - solver fixes: arb Jacobians in the held-angle sweeps; Levenberg-Marquardt candidates in q786/q789

1. The held-angle and held-mass solvers of the q738 family (q738, q772, q774, q780, q781, q787, q791 and their copies) build the
   finite-difference Jacobian in float64 and solve it with numpy. Near events the soft direction (the ring's own harmonic K) has a
   singular value of order 1e-13 relative to the others, below float64 resolution, so Newton stalls at residuals 1e-9..1e-14. This
   matches the creeps recorded since 1272 (e.g. lam 0.02 held mass 7.8e-14, 1304; NPMLE s 2 split at 88.5 deg 1.7e-9, 1310).
   q787 and q791 now keep the Jacobian and its solve in arb at the working precision (arb_mat). First use: the s 2 split held at 88.5
   deg went from 1.7e-9 to 1.3e-11 (39 iterations), with D - C = +1.3e-14 at 89 deg, i.e. a held split at 88.5 deg is not a KKT state
   there. q781, q774, q793, q794 still carry the float64 solve.
2. q786 and q789 (arb Jacobians already) now try Levenberg-Marquardt steps (mu = 1e-2 ... 1e-14 times the largest diagonal of J^T J)
   whenever the damped Newton step lowers the sum of squares by less than a factor 4, and keep the best. On the stalled copying-ring
   starts the residual now falls, but only slowly (LFP eps 0.160: 7.6e-12 to 3.8e-12 in 5 iterations; s 2 fourteen-ring at eps 0.284:
   3.0e-11 to 2.75e-12 in 13), which looks like a residual floor with no root nearby.

copy the smooth density there (q796: the moment problem needs negative masses), so the copying view holds the count at 14; the
extremal rule (K 14 lost at 0.2911, above the observed K 12 loss) would put 16 there.

## Amendment 1314 (02 Oct 18:14) - a candidate unifying principle for the 1D and 2D laws (a hypothesis, with its cheapest test)

Reading NPMLE_DERIVATION.md (sections 1.2-1.3, the common leading phase law of capacity, LFP and NPMLE on an interval) next to the 2D
results: in both settings the KKT ripple at the lattice frequency is the comb smoothed by the Gaussian, and for an unperturbed comb
it puts the atoms at MINIMA of the KKT function (1D: "for the uniform comb (beta = sigma = 0), arg Ghat = 0, so the atoms are minima
of T", NPMLE_DERIVATION 1.3; 2D: a regular ring on the circle has D(mid) - D(atom) = +4 |slope| > 0, 1283). Something must flip the
ripple so that each atom sits at a maximum:
- 1D (interval, edge): the comb's own chirp turns the ripple's phase to pi: 4 alpha^2 beta = pi, i.e. rho^2 rho' = 1/(16 pi^2), and
  with the edge this integrates to rho^3 = (3/(16 pi^2)) d and K ~ 0.4002 L^(4/3).
- 2D (near-circular curve, no edge): the curvature forcing flips the ripple's amplitude: the net fundamental ripple is proportional
  to (c_K - b_K) times the harmonic-K response, valid while c_K > b_K (signs as in 1248), lost where c_K = b_K (the copying-ring
  form, 1297-1313).
Hypothesis (not a result): one principle, "every atom sits at a maximum of the fundamental comb ripple; a count change happens where
neither the chirp phase nor the external forcing can keep that true", with the 1D phase law and the 2D copying-ring condition as its
two limits.
Cheapest test that can fail: a circle of radius R with a small gap (an arc with two ends). Near each end the 1D edge law should hold
(rho^3 = (3/(16 pi^2)) d along the arc, d from the end, unit noise), and as the gap closes the count must diverge; the hypothesis says
how: the edge chirp law near the ends and a ring governed by the curvature condition away from them. Measurements to make: the atom
density against arc distance from the end at moderate R (does rho^3/d approach 3/(16 pi^2)?), and K against the gap. Needs a solver for
open curves (one mirror symmetry, end atoms at the two ends): to be built as q800 from q719's text.
Gates: no gate word used.

Setting, as in 2401.17084 (re-extracted by me from papers/bridge_cap2d3d/arxiv_2401.17084v1.pdf): C(rp, rm) = max over P_X with
X in E(rp, rm) of I(X; X + Z), Z a standard normal vector in R^2, E(rp, rm) the filled ellipse x1^2/rp^2 + x2^2/rm^2 <= 1.
The F scripts (F_cert.md, scripts F_core.py, F_kkt.py, F_ring32_cert.py; log F_work/ring32_cert.log), starting from the D
state (1329):
- Representation: D(q) = |q|^2/2 - E log S(q + Z), S(y) = sum_k w_k exp(<y, x_k> - |x_k|^2/2). One global trapezoid grid of log S per
  measure; rigorous error = discretisation bound on the strip |Im y_j| < a with a rp < pi/2 (there every term of S has argument below
  pi/2, so S has no zeros and |L| has an explicit bound) by Poisson summation and contour shift, per axis 2M/(e^{2 pi a/h} - 1)
  (Trefethen-Weideman 2014, Thm 5.1; statement as recalled, proof re-derived in F's file; the published statement is not yet
  extracted by me: UNCHECKED, check scheduled), plus explicit Gaussian tail bounds for the truncated grid; Cauchy estimates for
  derivatives along the curve.

  system (D - C at one atom per orbit, tangential derivatives, total mass); Krawczyk test on the box v^ +- 6.82e-66 passes
  (||I - Y J(B)|| = 8.97e-22): a unique exact KKT point in the box, 8 G orbits, pair at 2.5863554508 deg, no atom at t = 0 or pi/2,
  smallest mass >= 0.02588, C = 0.3906492301481608.
- Curve: on [0, pi/2] (D2 symmetry), 32 Taylor intervals of order 36 with Cauchy remainders, 230 pieces: D - C <= -1.74e-53 off
  neighbourhoods of the atoms; (D - C)'' <= -2.86e-47 on each neighbourhood containing its atom's box (value and slope vanish exactly
  at the exact atom). Certified violations: none. D - C at the major vertex, enclosed for every point of the box: -1.127604e-50.

  Krawczyk ok, curve ok, vertex enclosure -1.127604e-50).
- The interior lemma, by hand: Hess D(q) = I - Cov(x_K | q + Z) averaged over Z, where the covariance is that of the atom position
  under the posterior weights; Cov <= E[x x^T] <= max_k |x_k|^2 I, so Hess D >= (1 - max_k |x_k|^2) I. Here max |x_k|^2 = 0.99984 (the

## Amendment 1336 (02 Oct 21:12) - the trapezoid bound used in 1335 checked against the published statement

Trefethen, Weideman, "The Exponentially Convergent Trapezoidal Rule", SIAM Review 56(3) 385-458 (2014), PDF from the first author's
page (papers/cert/trefethen_weideman_sirev2014.pdf), my PyMuPDF extraction, Theorem 5.1: "Suppose w is analytic in the strip
|Im(x)| < a for some a > 0. Suppose further that w(x) → 0 uniformly as |x| → ∞ in the strip, and for some M, it satisfies
∫ |w(x + ib)| dx ≤ M for all b ∈ (−a, a). Then, for any h > 0, Ih ... satisfies |Ih − I| ≤ 2M/(e^(2πa/h) − 1)". This is the per-axis
bound the F scripts used (1335); the UNCHECKED label on it is removed. F's integrands (log S times Gaussian weights) are analytic in the
strip |Im y_j| < a with a rp < pi/2 and decay like Gaussians in it, so the hypotheses hold; the constant M is F's explicit bound
(F_cert.md 20:34), not re-derived by me.

## Amendment 1339 (02 Oct 21:30) - the three remaining bridges of the HIGHEST TARGET are exact identities onto problems whose blind predictions passed tonight

(1) Rational inattention. Jung, Kim, Matejka, Sims, "Discrete actions in information-constrained decision problems"
(papers/jung_kim_matejka_sims_discrete_actions.pdf, my PyMuPDF extraction): the problem maximises E U(X, Y) - lambda I(X; Y) over
joint laws with the state's prior fixed, and "When U(x, y) depends only on x −y and is maximized at x = y, the problem is the static
special case of what that literature calls rate-distortion theory." With U = -|x - y|^2, actions confined to a curve and lambda = T,
this is the rate-distortion Lagrangian of mass-constrained deterministic annealing at temperature T (Rose), whose KKT function is the
NPMLE one with sigma = sqrt(T/2) (1320). The DA bridge passed 5 of 5 blind events (K 8-16, 1320-1337), so the rational-inattention
problem with a Gaussian prior and an elliptical action set has the same count changes at lambda = T_c, by identity.
(2) Model selection. Mattingly, Transtrum, Abbott, Machta (papers/bridge2/arxiv_1705.01166.pdf, my extraction): "We advocate for the
prior which maximizes the mutual information between param- eters and predictions" and "The prior p⋆(θ) is almost always discrete".
For Gaussian observations x ~ N(theta, sigma^2 I / m) with theta on a curve, that prior is the capacity-achieving input of the
Gaussian channel with noise sigma/sqrt(m), i.e. the record's capacity problem with all lengths scaled by sqrt(m)/sigma. Tonight's
capacity results (lam 0.02 K 16 and K 18 blind; the certified rp 1.0 32-ring) transfer by this scaling.
(3) Minimax coding. By the redundancy-capacity theorem (Gallager 1979; Davisson, Leon-Garcia 1980; Haussler 1997, cited by Mattingly
et al. as ref. 40), the minimax redundancy of the family {N(theta, I) : theta in the set} equals the capacity of the channel theta -> x,
and the least favourable (maximin) prior is the capacity-achieving input; the original statements are not re-extracted here
(UNCHECKED as quotes; the theorem is standard).
Status of the HIGHEST TARGET's bridge list: capacity (blind passes), LFP (blind pass K 12), NPMLE = rate-distortion (blind passes
K 12-18), deterministic annealing (5/5), rational inattention (identity with RD/DA), model selection (identity with capacity),
minimax coding (identity with capacity). Each bridge is either tested directly or is the same computation as a tested one. What
stays open is the law itself across 1D and 2D (BACKLOG 40) and the edge layers in 2D.
Gates: no gate word used.

linear-response offset), which places every scored event near the circle; or (B) an instability of the atom at the minor vertex of
the 1D-centre type (Y birth or Y split, the chirp-phase events of 1D, 1327), which ends the ring earlier than (A) predicts.
Evidence collected after the fact: lam 0.02 K 20 (Y split, lost 2.2 % earlier in eps than (A); 1341-1344); the G ellipse family
at rp 3 and 5 (G_family.md; every count change at t = pi/2, alternating Y births and splits, (A) loses the ring 1.5-3.2 % too
late, the gap shrinking with K). In 1D only (B) exists, since the formal density carries no content at the centre (1327).
What it needs to become a law: a criterion, computable before solving, for which of (A) and (B) comes first, and a value for (B)
(the 1D phase constant +0.171 or its 2D analogue). Test plan: the G scripts (BACKLOG 40) works on the collapse of K across the ellipse family
and on this criterion; any criterion is registered here before it is scored.
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 1367 (03 Oct 02:55) - where the factorial growth of the formal series comes from: a_k = d_k / J_2k with d_k geometric

From q764's own output at R 1.0 (q764_R1.0_N160_D8.json stores a_k and J_2k; inline check 02:5x): d_k = a_k J_2k (the shape forcing
of harmonic 2k before division by the circle integral) is geometric, |d_k|^(1/k) = 0.204 (k 1), 0.087 (8), 0.048 (16), 0.0458 (40),
0.0414 (96), 0.0394 (160), with successive ratios d_k/d_(k-1) 0.0414-0.0419 between sign changes (k 96-160) and sign changes every
15-17 steps (the lobes). J_2k(2k)!/(R^2/2)^(2k) falls from 0.51 (k 1) to 2.5e-10 (k 160). So the (k!)^2-type growth of a_k (1273)
is entirely the division by J_2k, the circle's radial integral at harmonic 2k (the deconvolution step), and the shape enters only
through a geometric rate near 0.04 with a slow rotation of period about 32 in k. Consequence for the count past the first lobe (1364):
K is fixed by where 2 |d_k| (eps/2)^k / J_2k reaches order one, i.e. by the asymptotics of J_2k(R) (a known Bessel-type integral) and
by the rate rho(R) of d_k; this is the route to the eps -> 0 constant and to its rp dependence without fitting. The rp 0.8 and 1.2
grids (q790, 26 and 34 pairs, 640 and 768 bits, 128 and 160 angles; the 96-angle, 256-bit setting of 1364 cannot resolve more than
24 pairs: aliasing and probe precision, the runs of 02:50 failed with singular Jacobians) are running.

## Amendment 1378 (03 Oct 06:19) - the 1D count law is one edge's profile integrated: the interval's bulk follows the half-line gap profile g(x) ~ 3.70 x^(-1/3) at depth x, and 2 * integral of 1/g gives 0.405 a^(4/3) against the record's 0.4002

Three candidate mechanisms for the bulk densification of 1377 were written (two edges glued into one profile; edge-generated formal
content decaying inward; an envelope-against-ripple balance, which a rough estimate already gives as log-type spacing, not a^(-1/3)); the
cheapest, the first, was run on stored data.
Half-line capacity optimum (centre_scripts/c50_cap_D100_norefit.json, stage D 98, 111 atoms to depth 112): gap g at depth x and
g x^(1/3): 1.5455 at 12.7 (3.604), 1.3460 at 19.9 (3.645), 1.2514 at 25.0 (3.661), 1.1420 at 33.4 (3.677), 1.0775 at 40.0 (3.686),
1.0004 at 50.4 (3.695), 0.9449 at 60.1 (3.702), 0.8586 at 79.9 (3.698): g ~ 3.70 x^(-1/3), the constant still drifting up by about
0.1 % per 10 in depth.
Against the interval optima of 1377: the half-line gap averaged over the depths of the interval's middle third (2a/3 .. a) is about
1.32 at a 25.13 and 1.21 at a 33.51; the interval's middle-third gaps are 1.344 and 1.228 (1.5-2 % sparser, the two edges' mutual
influence). The first five gaps from each edge are the half-line's to every printed digit.
So, to 1-2 %, the interval is two half-lines glued at the centre, and its count is K ~ 2 integral_0^a dx/g(x) = (3/2) a^(4/3)/3.70 =
0.405 a^(4/3) (a the half-width), 1.3 % above the record's 0.4002 a^(4/3) (consistent with the constant's upward drift toward about
3.75). The 1D count law therefore reduces to a single edge's chirp profile g ~ c x^(-1/3) (the record's chirp-phase law), and the 2D arcs
(the E scripts, 1372) inherit that profile with a curvature correction c_j/RC^2. Closed curves have no edge; their count comes from the
formal series (1364-1370). What a single law must still supply: why one edge's profile has local frequency growing as x^(1/3), in the
same copying terms that give the closed-curve count.

2019, as quoted by the referee; not yet re-extracted by me), and that the interior lemma of 1335 needs max |x_k|^2 < 1, so the rp 3
family was never shown to be the filled-ellipse optimum.

  +3.3e-2 at s 0.2; negative from s 0.4 outward (-3.9e-3 at s 0.995). So D > C inside the ellipse: this ring is the optimum of the
  curve-restricted problem only, and the filled-ellipse optimum at this point has mass in the interior (at or near the centre).

  applies there, max |x_k|^2 < 1).

reads of 1346-1347, 1352-1353 at rp 3 and rp 5) are tests of the copying law for the capacity problem whose input is confined to the

## Amendment 1407 (03 Oct 14:36) - the formal density gives the capacity itself to about 1e-10; via the minimax duality its output density is an upper-bound certificate

(1) Measured (q816 now prints C_formal = the mean of r(z) = -int phi_2(y - z) log p_f(y) dy on the curve; the D convention of the solvers
subtracts the entropy log(2 pi e) = 2.8378770664093453 of the noise): rp 3, rm 2.048089886719: C_formal - log(2 pi e) = 1.288761805212
(M 10) and 1.288761805260 (M 8), ring C 1.288761805372 (ball arithmetic state, G_work/arb18/trk/); rm 2.095269101562: 1.299969614975 (M 10),
ring 1.299969614855 (rp3k20check state). Agreement 1.2e-10 to 1.6e-10, at eps/rp = 0.32, with a formal density that is not positive
(min f -0.62). At M 12 and 14 the Newton solve for the density does not converge (harmonic residual 0.04-0.06; the series is past
its lobe), so the useful truncation is near K/2, the copying convention.
(2) Why it can be a certificate (not computed yet): by the minimax (dual) characterisation of capacity, every output density q gives
C <= sup_x D(P_Y|x || q); with q = p_f, the formal density smoothed by the noise, a probability density whenever p_f > 0 (its integral is
1 because f integrates to 1), the bound is C_formal - log(2 pi e) plus the largest ripple of D(.||p_f) over the input set, i.e. of order
the residual harmonics (1e-9 here). With the ring's mutual information as the lower bound, capacity is pinned to about 1e-9 from a
float64 Newton on ten coefficients. For the filled ellipse the supremum includes the interior, which is below the curve exactly when
the centre excess of 1403 is negative. A rigorous version needs sup_x and p_f > 0 in ball arithmetic. Literature for the duality
bound itself: classical (Csiszar-Korner; Kemperman); UNCHECKED here, not claimed as new.
(3) Reading: the copying description now covers three quantities of the optimum, each from the same smooth formal density: the ring
(quadrature), its loss (Verblunsky coefficient), and the capacity and centre excess (the density's own value), the last two to 7-10
digits. Paper A2: a remark in Section VII.
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 1416 (03 Oct 15:17) - second-round referee on paper A2 (RQ): verdicts verified and applied; the duality remark corrected (positivity of the output law needs f >= 0)

Report: review/paperA2_R2/REPORT_A2R2.md (fresh reader; condensed by me). The referee reproduced
independently the rp 3 ring capacities and centre values, the circle zero (2.453390) and two Table II entries (2.4085664, 2.1874224).
Verdicts, each checked:
- E3 duality: CONFIRMED and important. The output law of a density f on the curve is a probability density on R^2 only if f >= 0 (in the
  far field q behaves like f at the extreme point of the curve in that direction), i.e. exactly when f is admissible; at rp 3 the M 10
  density has min f -0.62/-0.63, so C_f there is an approximation and not a bound, which also explains C_f exceeding the (P2) optimum by
  1.2e-10 at rm 2.095270 (no contradiction). The supremum must range over the input set. The rigorous sandwiches of 1410-1412 used the
  128-point sampled input with positive weights (min f 0.17-0.97 at rp 1, M 4), a valid input, so they stand; A2 now says so and cites
  Thangaraj-Kramer-Bocherer arXiv 1511.08742 (abstract read in our local copy: 'A dual capacity expression is used to derive analytic
  capacity upper bounds for scalar and vector AWGN channels'); A1 cites it too.
- E2: the value at rm 2.095270 is the capacity of (P2) only: CONFIRMED, stated.
- B1 truncation: CONFIRMED; A2 now states the K/2 truncation for the rule and the residuals at K + 2, K + 4 for the correction, and
  defines c_(K+2) as the effective coefficient -r_(K+2)/L_(K+2,K+2) (B_derivation.md (c2)). B2 (pi_(K-2) q_4 term, O(eta)): applied.
  B4 (relative vs absolute): CONFIRMED, now absolute |h_j|. B5 ('ball arithmetic' for the formal density gives no rigour): CONFIRMED,
  reworded ('high-precision arithmetic', quadrature not enclosed, ill-conditioning stated).
- A1-A5: the 0.13 % claim now holds for every row (36-ring -0.05..+0.12 % after 1413) and the abstract says one kind is open; row 9
  printed +0.07..+0.08 % (CONFIRMED: +0.066..+0.075); row 1 as a bracket; '34- and 36-rings were solved'; 9.4e-5; 'computed by the rule'
  for K 16-28.
- C1-C4: the eps^(-1/2) law labelled heuristic and asymptotic; exponent 0.59 from K 38 to 320 (CONFIRMED from the printed values); rho
  'asymptotically geometric, about 0.05 near k 20'; the J_2k error moves K by about 1 %; at K 320 eq. (2) with its finite-K factor gives
  8.9-9.5, matching the series 8.9 (the referee's like-for-like comparison, accepted; the earlier 'not agreement' sentence removed);
  'infinitely many intervals' now names the extrapolation of the sign pattern beyond k 160.
- D1: abstract states the segment test was run with the targets known and gives 0.04 % and 0.8 %; the rm extrapolation described as
  linear from nearby values. D2 / 3.2: A^(4/3) 'observed', Abbott-Machta 'derived non-rigorously'.
- E1: the rp 2.8 values printed to 7 digits (-7.240857e-5, +1.058679e-4, as in 128 bits); the agreement is 5e-8 absolute. E4, E5, E6:
  the centre-first observation limited to rp 2.8 and 3; the rp <= 2.4534 statement is now a conjecture from the stated grids, with
  what was not checked; at rp 3 the rm -> 0 limit is the small negative scalar value (-3e-4 at rm 0.005). E7: the suppression factor
  called qualitative. F1: the interior grid stated (s <= 0.995). F2: the quadrature channel's input described correctly.
- Citations: DAPS 2.454 now 'refined to 2.4534 (rounds to 2.453)'; the nine digits of 1.665925641 attributed to DAPS; r_m < r_p added to
  the finiteness statement; Rassouli-Clerckx 2016 and Dytso-Goldenbaum-Poor-Shamai 2019 added (from DBK's list); Wu-Verdu 2010 and
  Lapidoth-Moser 2003 not added yet (UNCHECKED, for the literature step).
- Title changed to 'A Szego-Quadrature Conjecture for Optimal Discrete Inputs on Closed Curves, with a Blind Record'
  (placeholder); the form label 'C' in Table I renamed 'S' (it clashed with the capacity); Fig. 1 caption explains the guide lines and

## Amendment 1432 (03 Oct 16:25) - the nested-copying offset derived (post hoc) as the inner curve's ellipticity in planar moments; method registered for blind tests at rp 3.6 and 4.15

Observation (16:2x, from the logged q822 states): at each loss the offset matches eps = a_1/a_0 of the inner formal curve
rho(th) = a_0 + a_1 cos 2th: pair losses at rp 3.5 / 3.7 / 3.85 / 4.0 have eps 0.60 / 2.43 / 4.1 / 6.5 % against offsets 0.58 /
2.0-2.4 / 4.3 / 6.8 %.
Derivation (heuristic, first order in eps): a small inner ring acts on the output through its planar moments; the 2k-th angular harmonic
of the output near the ring is led by the complex moment int rho^2k e^(2ikth) dmu, and the radial part by int rho^2k dmu. A pair at
(+-a, 0) has quadrupole / second moment Q/R = 1 at any radius; an X + Y quartet has hexadecapole / fourth moment H/R4 = 1 for any radii
and masses. For g = 1 + d_1 cos 2th + d_2 cos 4th on rho = a_0 + a_1 cos 2th: Q/R = d_1/2 + eps (1 - d_1^2/2) and
H/R4 = d_2/2 + eps d_1 (1 - d_2) + O(eps^2). Copying written in the plane (the ring is lost where the density's normalized K-th moment
reaches the ring's) gives the loss at d_1 = 2 (1 + eps) for the pair and d_2 = 2 (1 + eps d_1) for the quartet: the offsets eps and
eps d_1, both set by the inner curve's ellipticity, which the outer ellipse imposes (hence a function of rp).
Post hoc check (centre_scripts/q824_moment_offset.py on the existing logs; first-order and exact-moment versions): rp 3.5 pair: 3.409711
(first order), 3.409709 (exact) against the pair model's loss 3.40971; rp 3.7 quartet: 3.440720 / 3.440635 against (3.4405, 3.441]
(Hessian zeros 3.4406-3.4408). The other four points need logs that extend past the corrected crossing (running, ext logs).
REGISTERED METHOD for blind tests at rp 3.6 and rp 4.15 (q822 runs started 16:25, no pair or quartet model run at these rp): the
predicted pair loss is the rm where the exact-moment pair condition of q824 (MI 1 log) crosses zero; the predicted quartet loss is the
rm where the exact-moment quartet condition (MI 2 log) crosses zero. Bands: +-15 % of the offset's own size in rm, minimum +-4e-4 (the
largest post hoc miss so far is about 2e-4 at the quartet of rp 3.7). The numbers will be appended before q821/q823 are run there.
Gates: no gate word used.

triangularly: z = A e^(it) + B e^(-it) with A, B = (rp +- rm)/2, so once the harmonics below K are copied,
M_K(ring) - M_K(f) = (A^K + B^K)(b_K - c_K)/2; the boundary rule b_K = c_K is the same as equal K-th complex moments. On a free inner
curve the polar angle is not that coordinate, and the rule holds in its moment form. So the copying law of the record reads, at every
level tested, as: an optimal K-ring is the quadrature of its formal density that matches the complex moments below K, and it is lost
where the K-th normalized moment of the density reaches the ring's. Two levels inside the region, boundary rings on curves; one family
(the filled ellipse, rp 3.5-4.15).

## Amendment 1481 (03 Oct 20:56) - PRE-REGISTERED (candidate C2): the NPMLE edge law on a disc; the curvature correction to f0/e is the 1D edge defect over R

Problem: data uniform on the disc of radius R in the plane (density f0 = 1/(pi R^2)), unit Gaussian noise, the population NPMLE (maximise
L = int f0 log m over the disc, m = G * phi). By rotation symmetry the optimum is a set of rings (and possibly a centre atom). No 2D
NPMLE has been computed in this project; the solver (centre_scripts/q845_npmle_disc.py) is written after this entry.
Derivation (mine, sketched, the 2D version of 702/717): Danskin in R gives dL/dR = (2/R)(log m(R) - L); with L = log f0 + f0 Gt,
Gt(R) = int over the disc of log(m/f0), this is the exact identity log(m(R)/f0) = -1 + Gt'(R)/(2 pi R). A straight edge reduces exactly to
the 1D half-line problem (translation invariance along the edge, the Gaussian kernel factorises), so Gt(R) = 2 pi R D + E0 + E1/R + ...
with D = -0.304944 the 1D per-edge defect (702, 706: G = -0.609888223692 for two edges). Hence
  R (log(m(R)/f0) + 1) = D - E1/(2 pi R^2) + (bulk ripple terms, expected below 1e-6 relative).
PREDICTIONS, registered before any 2D solve:
P1 (identity, a numerics check): log(m(R)/f0) + 1 equals Gt'(R)/(2 pi R) by a centred difference in R (R +- 0.05) to 2 % of its value
   at R = 10 and 20.
P2 (law, parameter-free): R (log(m(R)/f0) + 1) at R = 10, 15, 20, 30 lies within 0.03 of D = -0.30494 for R >= 15, and its distance
   to D does not grow from R = 15 to R = 30. FAIL otherwise. (Reading of f0/e alone, i.e. no 1/R term, would give 0 for this quantity;
   a defect of the 2D edge different from the 1D one would give a different limit.)
Solver acceptance (stated now): KKT function int f0 k_r / m <= 1 + 1e-9 on a radial grid to R + 4, equality at the rings to 1e-10,
mass 1 to 1e-12; the result is reported for each R only if accepted.
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 1485 (03 Oct 21:56) - quadrature record for 1484; the local edge law derived for any boundary; PRE-REGISTERED: the concave inner edge of an annulus (the edge value rises above f0/e)

(1) Quadrature, R = 33.5 at NQ 5000 (centre_scripts/q846_nq5000/R33.5.log): 22 rings, m(R)/f0 = 0.3645461232 as at NQ 3000 (10 digits),
R (log(m(R)/f0) + 1) = -0.304924; its polish stops at residual 1.4e-7 (not accepted at NQ 5000; the count and edge value agree).
(2) Derivation (mine, sketched). For data uniform on a region Omega (f0 = 1/|Omega|), move the boundary outward by delta_n(s). Danskin:
dL = f0 oint delta_n (log m(s) - L) ds; with L = log f0 + f0 Gt, Gt = int_Omega log(m/f0), and d log f0 = -f0 oint delta_n ds, this is
the exact identity  oint delta_n(s) [log(m(s)/f0) + 1] ds = dGt[delta_n]  for every deformation. If the edge layers are local,
Gt = oint (D + a kappa + b kappa^2 + ...) ds + (bulk terms), and with d(oint ds) = oint kappa delta_n ds, oint kappa ds fixed, and
delta(oint kappa^2 ds) = -oint (2 kappa'' + kappa^3) delta_n ds:
   log(m(s)/f0) + 1 = D kappa(s) - b (kappa(s)^3 + 2 kappa''(s)) + ...,
with D = -0.304944 (1D) and b = -0.024 from the disc fit (1482: R (log m/f0 + 1) - D = +0.024/R^2). In d dimensions kappa is the sum of
principal curvatures. kappa < 0 on a concave edge: there the edge value lies ABOVE f0/e.
(3) PRE-REGISTERED (solver: q847 = q846 with the data on an annulus R1 <= |y| <= R2, written after this entry): data uniform on the
annulus 10 <= |y| <= 30. Predictions for L(r) = log(m(r)/f0) + 1:
   outer edge r = 30 (kappa = +1/30): L = D/30 + 0.024/30^3 = -1.016591e-2, band +-3e-6;
   inner edge r = 10 (kappa = -1/10): L = -D/10 - 0.024/10^3 = +3.02544e-2, band +-3e-5 (higher orders scale as kappa^5 ~ 1e-5 x coefficient).
Sign test inside it: L(10) > 0 (edge value above f0/e). FAIL if outside either band. Acceptance as in 1481.
Gates: no gate word used.

that carry its outer ring (its fine grid covers only +-0.15 around coarse support points). Reading: the edge value responds at first
order to how the outer support is spread along the edge, while the likelihood responds at second order, so a grid optimum that is
1e-6 short in likelihood can be 10 % off in the edge value. q849 is not used for any test.

carries a ripple from the nearest atoms. The test of the local law must use the low angular harmonics (0, 2, 4) of L(s) along the
whole edge against those of D kappa(s), with a solver whose KKT holds on a full fine grid of the support band. Already separated:

## Amendment 1497 (03 Oct 22:31) - the NPMLE edge-DEPTH curvature coefficient derived from two 1D facts (post hoc on the disc), and PRE-REGISTERED for the ball and the annulus' inner edge (positions not yet looked at)

Derivation (mine, sketched). For the radial problem in d dimensions, with the data density per unit radius proportional to rho^(d-1)
and the large-argument shell kernel, the likelihood is that of a 1D problem with (i) data tilted toward the outer edge with log-slope
(d - 1)/R and (ii) a kernel phi(rho - r) (rho/r)^((d-1)/2) = phi(rho - r - (d - 1)/(2r)) x (1 + O(r^-2)): every shell acts as a 1D atom
moved outward by (d - 1)/(2R). With M the 1D NPMLE depth shift per unit log-slope of the data density (788: 0.6587 at t = 0.05, 0.6567
at t = 0.3; the edge atom moves toward an edge where the data thicken), the outer-ring depth is
   R - r_out = D_1 + (d - 1)(1/2 - M)/R + O(R^-2),   D_1 = 1.488 (1D uniform NPMLE edge depth, 788),
and on a concave inner edge of radius a the sign of the curvature term flips: r_in - a = D_1 + (d - 1)(M - 1/2)/a + O(a^-2).
(1) Disc, post hoc (outer-ring positions of q846 and q668 states had been printed, so not blind): fit a + b/R + c/R^2 over the 21
accepted states with R >= 15: a = 1.48756, b = -0.1554, c = -0.317 (largest residual 1.5e-6); derived b = 1/2 - M = -0.1587 (-0.1567 with
the t = 0.3 value): agreement about 2 %. The window R >= 10 gives b = -0.147. Reading: 1020's capacity remark ("the naive (d - 1)/(2r)
estimate gives 0.5, three quarters of 0.662") had the kernel half; the other half is the 1D tilt response. For capacity the wall is
pinned at the boundary, so the kernel shift does not move depths relative to the wall at first order, and 0.6582 would then be minus the
1D capacity response to the tilt that the radial weight induces (an input-cost tilt log r, not a data tilt): not computed here.
(2) PRE-REGISTERED, from states on disk whose shell/ring positions I have not looked at:
  B (ball, q848 states R = 8, 10, 12, 15, 20, 25, 30): fit a + b/R + c/R^2 over R >= 12: b = 2 (1/2 - M) = -0.3174 +- 0.02 and
    a = 1.4876 +- 0.002.
  I (annulus 10..30, q847 state): first ring above the inner edge: r_in - 10 in [1.497, 1.507] (first order 1.50343; with an even
    second-order term of the disc's size, 1.50023); last ring below the outer edge: 30 - r_out = 1.48191 +- 0.0005.

## Amendment 1499 (03 Oct 22:32) - PRE-REGISTERED: capacity's measured curvature coefficient 0.6582 (1031) is the 1D capacity's response to a linear input reward; test on a 1D tilted capacity solved for the first time (no solver exists yet)

Derivation (mine, sketched). On the disc, h(Y) = H(mu) + E log(2 pi |Y|) with mu the density of |Y|; mu is a 1D convolution whose kernel is
phi shifted outward by 1/(2r), and E log |Y| = E log r + O(r^-2). So near the wall, to first order in 1/R, C_2D is a 1D capacity with the
linear input reward log r ~ const + (r - R)/R, i.e. reward slope t = (d - 1)/R increasing toward the wall; the kernel shift moves wall and
rings together and does not change depths measured from the wall at first order. Hence: the 2D depth shift per unit curvature (0.6582
per (d - 1), 1031, measured on 1 Oct) should equal the 1D capacity depth shift per unit reward slope.
Test problem: maximise I(X; Y) + t E[X] over X in [-A, A], unit Gaussian noise (KKT: i(x) + t x <= C' with equality on the support). The
right wall sees the reward rising toward it, the left wall falling. Solver centre_scripts/q850_cap1d_tilt.py (written after this entry:
Blahut-Arimoto on a fine grid for the support, then Newton on atoms and wall masses, KKT checked on a 0.001 grid).
PREDICTIONS (A = 16): with depth_R = A - (largest interior atom), depth_L = (smallest interior atom) + A:
  T1: t = 0: depth_R = depth_L = 2.7188 +- 0.002 (the 1D half-line depth 2.718843; control).
  T2: (depth_R - depth_L)/(2 t) = +0.6582 +- 0.015 at t = 0.02 and at t = 0.05 (the right atom deeper).
  T3: (depth_R + depth_L)/2 - 2.7188 smaller than 0.1 t (the response is odd in t at first order).
FAIL if T2 fails at either t. A FAIL would mean 0.6582 is not this tilt response (the mapping is missing a first-order piece).
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 1509 (03 Oct 23:05) - PRE-REGISTERED (candidate C6): capacity's edge strip carries to the disc; the C values of the 1 Oct disc states are read only after this entry

Record: the 1D capacity expansion e^(C + h(Z)) = 2A + beta, beta = 3.98160794709, exact to 1e-9 on blind states (726): an edge strip of
width beta/2 per edge. A search of the log for this constant or a strip after amendment 24000 finds nothing in 2D.
Reading to be tested (same local-edge argument as 1485/1504: a straight edge of the plane is the 1D half-line problem): for an input

## Amendment 1519 (03 Oct 23:31) - PRE-REGISTERED: capacity's mean-curvature coefficient a = 1.85 (1516) from the 1D strip's response to a linear input reward

Derivation (mine, sketched; the capacity version of 1517's radial reduction). On the d-ball, h(Y) = -D(mu || rho^(d-1) d rho) + log S_d with
mu the density of |Y|; the shell kernel is phi shifted outward by (d - 1)/(2r), so in shifted coordinates the wall sits at
R' = R + (d - 1)/(2R) and the reference measure rho^(d-1) is a reward of slope t = (d - 1)/R toward the wall. If the 1D strip at a wall
toward which a linear reward t x rises is b(t) = beta/2 + k t + O(t^2), the effective radius is R_eff = R' + b(t) and
e^(h(Y)) = V_d R_eff^d gives S(A) = beta/2 + (d - 1)(1/2 + (beta/2)^2/2 + k)/A + ..., i.e.
   a = 1/2 + (beta/2)^2/2 + k = 2.48165 + k.

order t^2 (2A + beta); two widths separate it from k2. Data: A = 16 (q850_seed19_fine.log and q850_seed19.log, t = 0.005-0.05, already

## Amendment 1538 (04 Oct 00:35) - PRE-REGISTERED: the remainder after the coupling (1534, 1536) is the tilt dependence of the 1D finite-width deviation

Idea. Through the radial reduction the shell is a 1D strip whose reference measure has log-slope t = (d - 1)/R_mid, i.e. the 1D capacity
with a linear input reward t x (q850). 1533/1535 used the coupling at t = 0. The next term keeps everything 1D:
   P2 = P1 + S_mid [eps_t(A) - eps_0(A)],   A = W/2,   S_mid = 2 pi R_mid (2D) or 4 pi R_mid^2 (3D),
   eps_t(A) = Z_1D(A, t) - Z_inf(A, t),   Z_1D = e^(C(t) + h_1) (C(t) the printed I + tE of q850),
   Z_inf = [e^(t (A + b_R)) - e^(-t (A + b_L))]/t,   b_R = beta/2 + k t + k2 t^2,   b_L = beta/2 - k t + k2 t^2,   k = -0.63226, k2 = 0.049 (1520).
No parameter is fitted. The observed values were scored in 1534 and 1536, so this test is blind only in that eps_t does not exist yet
and the formula and criterion are fixed here.
Runs (q850 unchanged, BA seed, t in {0, t_target}, logs centre_scripts/q850_tilt1538/, started after this entry): the decisive widths
of 1534/1536 at A = 1.5-6.5 with t_target = (d - 1)/R_mid: 2D a = 10 (6 widths, t 0.069-0.087), 2D a = 20 (7 widths, t 0.039-0.047),
3D (10 widths, t 0.075-0.093). Accepted rows only (residual <= 1e-10, KKT <= 1e-9).
Floors: the RMS of obs - P1 is 6.41e-2 (2D a = 10) and 3.31e-2 (2D a = 20), equal to their local-term bands (0.072, 0.033), so the 2D
sets cannot show a reduction beyond the uncertainty of the disc constants; in 3D it is 2.95 against a band of 0.64.
H_tilt (verdict on the 3D set): RMS(obs - P2) <= 0.5 x RMS(obs - P1) = 1.47 over the accepted decisive widths. FAIL otherwise. The 2D
sets are reported: consistent if RMS(obs - P2) <= RMS(obs - P1) + 0.5 x base.

## Amendment 1554 (04 Oct 01:27) - BACKLOG 55 done: rigorous capacity sandwiches for rp > 1 (the interior step no longer needs convexity), at rp 1.2, 1.5, 2.0; the A1 point reproduced exactly

Interior step (design B55_interior_design.md). For a Gaussian-mixture output q of an input inside the ellipse, the standard
identities grad D(x) = x - E[E(X | Y)] and Hess D(x) = I - E[Cov(X | Y)] (Y ~ N(x, I)) give |grad D| <= |x| + rp and
(1 - rp^2) I <= Hess D <= I. With (a) the curve check of q817 (D < U on the curve) and (b) a certified lower bound gamma on the outward
derivative g'(1) = z . grad D(z) along the curve, Hess D <= I gives D(s z) <= D(z) - g'(1)(1 - s) + rp^2 (1 - s)^2/2 < U for
0 < 1 - s < 2 gamma/rp^2 (the band); (c) the rest (s <= s_b) is covered by a Cartesian grid with ball values of D and the Lipschitz
bound 2 rp. Code: F_m1.py (grid functions M1 = E(X | Y = y) on F_core's grid; g'(1) Taylor series with the same weights as
Lam; strip bound rp/cos(a rp) for the quadrature error); centre_scripts/q860_formal_sandwich_rp.py (TEXT COPY of q817 plus (b), (c)).
Check of F_m1 (F_m1_check.py, rp 1.5, rm 1.45): g'(1) from M1 equals a ball-arithmetic central difference of D(s z) at
s = 1 +- 1e-6 to 1.4e-13 at five angles.
Runs (formal density M 4, N = 128 points, 256 bits, h 1/16, grid 577; strip a < pi/(2 rp); logs centre_scripts/q860_runs/):
