## Amendment 1569 (04 Oct 02:44) - one frame for the three problems (the LFP deficit is exactly a Fisher information, checked to 2e-12); a corner test set aside; the grid LFP solver checked on a square against the exact product value

(1) Frame (paperA/A4_why_widened.md). In all three problems the law pi on Omega enters through p = pi * phi only: capacity maximises
the entropy h(p) (e^(C + h_d) is the entropy power), the NPMLE maximises int_Omega f0 log p, and for the LFP the Bayes risk of the
posterior mean is B = d - I(p), the Fisher information of the output (Tweedie's formula delta = y + grad log p and Stein's identity;
Brown's identity, reference UNCHECKED). Check on the q861 disc state m = 2.5 (1558): I(p) = 0.6879937245 (radial quadrature, 3000
nodes), 2 - I = 1.3120062755, recorded B = 1.3120062755, difference 2.0e-12. So the LFP deficit is min I(pi * phi) over pi on Omega;
over densities supported in a domain the minimum of I is 4 lambda_1 (ground state), which is why a Dirichlet eigenvalue appears; that
the Gaussian smoothing displaces the effective boundary by the 1D constant delta is the conjecture tested in 1557-1568.
(2) Corner test set aside (exploratory). For an equilateral triangle of inradius 3, the sharp widening (edges moved out by delta,
exact 4 lambda_1 = 16 pi^2/(9 (3 + delta)^2) = 0.435449; centre_scripts/q864d_dirichlet_triangle.py reproduces it to 0.02 % after
Richardson) and the rounded widening (all points within delta; 4 lambda_1 = 0.440103 after Richardson) differ by 1.07 %, the size of the
finite-size effects seen on discs (up to 2.7 %, 1564): the LFP cannot separate them at these sizes, so no test is registered.
(3) Instrument check on a cornered domain. The LFP on the square [-m, m]^2 is exactly the product of two 1D LFPs (additive loss,
product region), so 2 - B* = 2 (1 - r*_1D(m)). centre_scripts/q863c_lfp_grid2d_polygon.py (q863 with polygon masks), square m = 2.5,
8000 iterations: 2 - B* in [0.591873, 0.592119], containing 2 x 0.295989 = 0.591978 (q862, 1556); midpoint ratio 1.00003.
Gates: no gate word used.

|Y|^2 ~ d (1 + mu), the mean cosine I_{d/2}/I_{d/2-1}(x) -> z/(1 + sqrt(1 + z^2)) with z = 2x/d. Then r(m)/d -> mu/(1 + mu) and
r(0)/d -> mu A0^2 with A0 = sqrt(mu)/(1/2 + sqrt(1/4 + mu)); r(0) = r(m) gives mu^2 = 1/2 + sqrt(1/4 + mu), i.e. mu (mu^3 - mu - 1) = 0:
mu = rho = 1.324717957 (the plastic number), and the Bayes risk at the threshold is B/d -> rho/(1 + rho) = 1/rho^2 = 0.56984. At this
order r(tau)/d on tau = t^2/d in [0, rho] equals 0.56984 at both ends and is lower inside (minimum 0.4956 at tau 0.593), so the first
violation is at the centre. Data: m^2 - rho d = -0.208010, -0.293227, -0.333774, -0.355975, -0.369570, -0.378617, -0.389779 at d 1-6,

## Amendment 1598 (04 Oct 05:26) - PRE-REGISTERED: the curvature coefficient kappa(m) as the derivative in d at d = 1 equals the kappa(m) read in d = 2-5

q868's kernel takes any real d (Gamma(d/2) (2/x)^nu ive(nu, x), nu = d/2 - 1). At fixed m between two 1D events the support
structure does not change, so the LF state at d = 1 + eps follows from the 1D state by solve_inner (no event in between for small eps).
Define kappa_1(m) = (offset_d(m) - offset_1(m)) (m + delta)/(d - 1) at d = 1.05 and 1.10 (offset_d = 2 j_{d/2-1,1}/sqrt(d - B) - m,
j the first zero of J_{d/2-1}; at d = 1 this is pi/sqrt(1 - B) - m). PREDICTION (not computed): at the midpoints of the 1D event
intervals with m in [4.4, 7.3], kappa_1(m) lies within 0.02 of the mean of the d = 2-5 values of 1591 (1) at the same m (each d's
values linearly interpolated in m), and the d = 1.05 and 1.10 values agree to 0.005 (linearity in d - 1). This tests whether the
(d - 1) excess is a curvature response that is analytic at d = 1, the reading L of 1590 needs; it does not decide L against S.
Instrument: centre_scripts/q876_kappa_d1.py (1D states from the 1D event states of q866/q868, moved to the midpoints by solve_inner).
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 1609 (04 Oct 08:40) - the literature check: every reference of both papers checked and reported as printed; the certificate's quadrature lemma against the code (in advance of the second referee's report)

(1) Literature check, 4 Oct about 08:4x: all references of both papers (the list UNCHECKED_REFERENCES_2026-10-04.md: 20 in paper 1,
9 in paper 2, including the Marchand-Perron venue question and PPV 2010) were checked and are correct as printed. With amendment
1608 (the recomputation of every number) both clauses of the Acknowledgment's AI paragraph now rest on those checks. A note at the
head of each bibliography says the remaining UNCHECKED comments are historical; comments are stripped from
the arXiv sources.
(2) The second referee's working notes (review/paper1_R2/CHECKPOINT.md, 08:38) question Lemma 1: positivity of Re S shown for real q
only, while App. A uses the lemma at complex q (Cauchy discs of radius 0.5 and 1). Checked against the code before the report arrives:
F_core.py strip_consts (l.166-173) asserts a r_p < pi/2 and bounds L = log S in the strip |Im y_j| < a of the INTEGRATION
variable y; S(y) = sum w_k exp(<y, x_k> - |x_k|^2/2) does not depend on q. A complex q enters only through the Gaussian factor
phi(y - q), whose growth in the strip is the factor exp((a + sigma)^2/2 + sigma^2/2) in quad_err (l.150-163, line 155), and the
Cauchy-disc calls pass sigma = r_p sinh(rho) to that factor (cauchy_coef_err, l.176-183). So the positivity condition is a r_p < pi/2
(here 1.45 < pi/2) whatever the imaginary part of q; the code matches the lemma. The paper should say this in one sentence, since a
careful reader asked. Verdict on the report item to follow in 1610 after the full report is read.
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 1611 (04 Oct 08:58) - second referee on paper 1 (RQ): every finding checked against the record and the code; the quadrature-lemma objection rests on a misreading of how the integral is computed (clarified in the paper); seven claim-evidence repairs; paper 1 rebuilt (13 pp)

Report saved verbatim: review/paper1_R2/REPORT_R2.md. Recommendation RQ.
Verdicts (each checked by me; numbers computed with py at 08:5x):
(1) M1, Lemma 1 at complex q: REJECTED in substance, ACCEPTED as a disclosure gap. The referee assumes S is evaluated at q + Z. The
code computes D(q) = |q|^2/2 + const - int phi(y - q) log S(y) dy: F_core.py weights() expands phi1(y_n - r_p cos(t0 + s)) as a
Taylor series at the REAL grid points y_n, log S is tabulated on the real grid (lam_grid), and quad_err carries the Gaussian growth
exp((a + sigma)^2/2 + sigma^2/2). So the strip condition a r_p < pi/2 (1.45 < pi/2) is on y only, whatever Im q is (1609 (2)). The
lemma now states the integral in this form and says why the condition does not involve q; App. A gives a = 1.45 for the curve step
too (F_ring32_cert.py l.17, l.128) and the Cauchy-disc data (rho = 1, |Im q_j| <= r_p sinh 1).
(2) M2, tail "of order": ACCEPTED; the explicit bound of quad_err (T0, T1, (1 + eta)c + 0.7979 + 0.484h) is now in the lemma.

(3) M5, uniqueness: ACCEPTED with a self-contained sentence (h(Y) strictly concave in the output law; the Gaussian characteristic
